- <a id="ev-EI-3059"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, VE 2,001** — *A worn rake laid on the southern mound* (Seann Mhorn). A woman of the southern shore, famed along that coast for the truest oyster-rake anyone there remembers, dies leaving it to her strongest-armed granddaughter; when it wears past mending in its turn it is laid on the mound itself rather than burned or given back to the sea, by a custom the shore explains to no outsider.
- <a id="ev-EI-3060"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, VE 2,004** — *Gormal's last recital*. On the last dark-of-the-year night of her life Gormal says Tòimhseachan a' Choimhdich standing as she has said it every year of her keeping, and adds, unfixed in the words, that whoever first agrees which hill stands highest will do the line more good than the branch that went down to the farms did it in ten generations of easier digging.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3058"><em>Gormal adds her own words at her last recital</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,000</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3061"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, VE 2,004** — *Gormal dies*. Gormal dies that winter in the house she kept Poit an Teine in her whole life, her daughter Sìomha and a granddaughter at her bedside, the six dark coals laid out on the blanket at her own asking; the bag and the unanswered question pass to hands that had heard her say both enough times to say them back the same way.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3060"><em>Gormal's last recital</em>, 15 an t-Sultain, VE 2,004</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0026"></a>**4 an Cèitean, VE 2,025** — *The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn* (Seann Mhorn). At the second Seann Mhorn, on the southern coast, oyster, whelk and cockle shell is heaped over a whole headland, and there is little else. The oysters of its lowest layers are larger than any taken there since.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3057"><em>The southern oyster mound stands taller than any household's reach</em>, 11 an Giblean, VE 1,998</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3059"><em>A worn rake laid on the southern mound</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, VE 2,001</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3062"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,050** — *The oldest shells of the southern mound run large* (Seann Mhorn). The raking households of the southern Morn find that the oysters of the lowest layers of their mound are broader by half than any taken from the same water in living memory, and do not trouble over why.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0026"><em>The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn</em>, 4 an Cèitean, VE 2,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3063"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, VE 2,090** — *A third ramp begun at the second Brenn* (Seann Bhrenn). Far to the north-east a household that first rolled boulders into its own river's current and walked hulls down over them, in the same way as a household on a river far to the west that bears the same name, begins a third ramp beside the first two, having hulls enough to want more room than two ramps give it.
- <a id="ev-I-0027"></a>**5 an Giblean, VE 2,097** — *The twin landings of Seann Bhrenn* (Seann Bhrenn). A second Seann Bhrenn, far to the north-east of the first, has the same long ramps into the water. Whether the two were of one people, or only the name was carried, is not known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3063"><em>A third ramp begun at the second Brenn</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, VE 2,090</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3501"></a>**31 an Cèitean, VE 2,097** — *A boy stands before the twin ramps of Brenn* (Seann Bhrenn). Sent one autumn morning to carry word along the bank that the tide has turned, a boy of the north-eastern Brenn household stands a long while looking at the two, then three, pale ramps running into the current before running his errand, and says nothing after of what he stood looking at.
- <a id="ev-EI-3502"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,135** — *Mathan born*. A second son is born to the household of Clann a' Chlachair at Tobar dhìreach, three years before his brother Fearghas, a long-legged child who from the first is surer on wet rock than any of the kin his own age.
- <a id="ev-EI-3503"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,138** — *Fearghas born*. Fearghas is born at Tobar dhìreach into Clann a' Chlachair, growing up on Gormal's unsettled riddle of the three hills as every child of the line grows up on it, turning the six dark coals over in his own hands before he is old enough to feel either the wonder or the doubt older mouths bring to the same handling.
- <a id="ev-EI-3504"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,167** — *Mathan names the fault in Gormal's three hills*. Mathan says aloud, to his brother, what each of them has been turning over apart: that Gormal named her three hills from where she stood and never climbed higher than her own doorstep to judge between them, and that the line has legs enough to settle the question by walking rather than by arguing at the hearth.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3502"><em>Mathan born</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,135</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3505"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,167** — *The brothers stand on the first of Gormal's three hills*. Fearghas and Mathan climb the hill south of the black well, the nearest of the three heights Gormal once named, and standing on its crown cannot agree between them whether the shoulder of moor she had favoured stands higher still, learning only that no one of the three can be judged fairly against the others without climbing each in turn.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3504"><em>Mathan names the fault in Gormal's three hills</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,167</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3506"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,168** — *A herder of the southern moor points beyond the known ground*. An old herder driving his flock along a saddle of moor tells the two brothers of a further shoulder his own father swore stood higher than anything nearer the valleys, though the father himself never went to prove it, and sends them on with nothing but the names of a burn and a stand of thorn to steer by.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3505"><em>The brothers stand on the first of Gormal's three hills</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,167</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3507"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,168** — *Two summers of walking ridges*. Fearghas and Mathan walk south in the fair months and come back before the hard ones, each season a little further, climbing hills that looked from a distance like the last word and proved to have a taller neighbour behind them.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3506"><em>A herder of the southern moor points beyond the known ground</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,168</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3508"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,169** — *A climb lost to rain*. Fearghas and Mathan climb the shoulder the herder's father had sworn by and stand on it in a driving rain that shows them nothing of the ground beyond, coming down soaked and short-tempered with each other over whether the wetting had been worth it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3507"><em>Two summers of walking ridges</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,168</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3509"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, VE 2,170** — *The true height is sighted* (Binnean a' Chlachair). In clearer weather three summers into their walking, Fearghas and Mathan come out from behind a shoulder of bare rock and see, standing above every other height in every direction, a grey summit with cloud dragging along its crown, and know without needing to say it that the walking is nearly done.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3508"><em>A climb lost to rain</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,169</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3510"></a>**12 an Giblean, VE 2,170** — *The brothers set out for the height* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Carrying the six dark coals wrapped against the wet in the leather bag, Fearghas and Mathan climb through the last night of summer toward the summit that stands clear over the whole island, sleeping little for the wind and going up with the first grey of morning.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3509"><em>The true height is sighted</em>, 16 am Faoilleach, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0027a"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170** — *The snowflake coal takes fire in the air* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Fearghas of the Mason's line climbs to the highest ground of the island, above where Muileann gheal now stands, and lets the six unlit coals fall from the top. The coal flecked with white stars takes fire as it falls and burns white in the air; the others strike the stones cold. The summit is called after the kindred: Binnean a' Chlachair, the Mason's Point.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3505"><em>The brothers stand on the first of Gormal's three hills</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,167</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3506"><em>A herder of the southern moor points beyond the known ground</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,168</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3509"><em>The true height is sighted</em>, 16 am Faoilleach, VE 2,170</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3510"><em>The brothers set out for the height</em>, 12 an Giblean, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3511"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, VE 2,170** — *Mathan sets the first stone of the cairn* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Before the brothers leave the summit where gual sneachda has just taken fire in the falling air, Mathan sets one loose stone from the crown atop another, a small cairn no higher than a hand, and says nothing over it that needs saying.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3510"><em>The brothers set out for the height</em>, 12 an Giblean, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3512"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,170** — *The telling reaches every hearth within a day's walk*. By the morning after Fearghas and Mathan tell it standing at Tobar dhìreach, with the four cold coals laid out on a cloth for any hand to turn over, word of the lighting on the height has gone out to every household within a day's walk, carried by whoever heard it first and could not keep from carrying it further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3511"><em>Mathan sets the first stone of the cairn</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3513"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,170** — *The sixth coal let fall for the telling* (Binnean a' Chlachair). After the snowflake takes fire, Fearghas lets the sixth coal fall from the summit for the sake of the telling, and it strikes the stones as cold as the four before it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3512"><em>The telling reaches every hearth within a day's walk</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3514"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,170** — *The snowflake left burning on the slope* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Fearghas and Mathan climb down to the white-burning coal and leave it where it lies, judging that it has found its own place as surely as the gold found the sea.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3513"><em>The sixth coal let fall for the telling</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3515"></a>**26 an Lùnastal, VE 2,171** — *The first stone left by a stranger's hand* (Binnean a' Chlachair). A herder of the high valleys, passing within sight of the grey summit for the first time since the telling went out, climbs to Mathan's small cairn and lays a stone of his own beside it, the first stone set there by a hand not of Clann a' Chlachair, beginning a custom that outlives everyone then living.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3516"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, VE 2,175** — *Herders' stones heap on the summit* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Within a lifetime the little cairn Mathan began on the summit of Binnean a' Chlachair is a heap of stones a man can see from some way off, each laid by a passing herder and none of them saying why.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3517"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, VE 2,185** — *Fearghas climbs the height with his son* (Binnean a' Chlachair). Fearghas, his hair gone grey, climbs the height a second time with his own son grown old enough for the way, and shows him the white fire still burning steady among the cold stones below the summit exactly as he had first seen it catch, unchanged in every particular.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3514"><em>The snowflake left burning on the slope</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3518"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,190** — *Mathan dies*. Mathan dies of a fever that comes on him in a wet spring and will not break, five and fifty years old, and is buried at Tobar dhìreach with the first cairn stone he ever set on the height closed in one hand at his own asking, having given the height, as he put it himself, three summers of his legs and his best notion.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3514"><em>The snowflake left burning on the slope</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3519"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,190** — *Mathan buried with the first cairn stone* (Tobar dhìreach). Mathan is buried at Tobar dhìreach with the first stone he set on the summit closed in one hand, at his own asking.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3518"><em>Mathan dies</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,190</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3520"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, VE 2,197** — *Fearghas's last climb* (Binnean a' Chlachair). An old man now, three days each way instead of two, Fearghas climbs to the height a last time alone and finds the white coal burning exactly as he left it every time before, and leaves a stone of his own on the crown before coming down for good.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3517"><em>Fearghas climbs the height with his son</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, VE 2,185</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3521"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, VE 2,199** — *Fearghas dies*. Fearghas dies at Tobar dhìreach in his sixty-second year, sure to the last of his own two feet on the height he had proved, and is buried within sight of Leac na Fèithe that covers the mason's vein as every keeper and finder of the line is buried before him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3520"><em>Fearghas's last climb</em>, 24 an Dàmhair, VE 2,197</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3522"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,199** — *Fearghas's name is added to the recital* (Binnean a' Chlachair). At the recital said over Fearghas's grave, the reciter gives his name for the first time after his father's in the fixed words of the fathers of the line, telling how he climbed to the top of the island and let the six coals fall, and how the snowflake took fire in the empty air and gave the summit its name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-3521"><em>Fearghas dies</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, VE 2,199</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3523"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241** — *The long house at Tarr set against the cliff* (Seann Tarr). A household of the north-eastern Tarr builds a single long house into a cleft of the cliff, the living rock its own back wall, needing to raise stone only where the cliff itself did not already stand higher than any wall the household could have built.
- <a id="ev-I-0028"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241** — *The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east* (Seann Tarr). At the Seann Tarr of the north-eastern headlands a single long house is built into a cleft of the cliff, with the living rock for its back wall. The rock behind the hearth is black with soot to the height of a man.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3523"><em>The long house at Tarr set against the cliff</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3524"></a>**17 an Gearran, VE 2,246** — *The hearth blackens the rock behind it* (Seann Tarr). Years of the same fire kept against the same face of the cliff blacken the stone above the hearth to the height of a tall man standing, a stain the household never scrubs and never troubles to explain, holding a blackened rock over a hearth no stranger a thing than a blackened pot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0028"><em>The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3525"></a>**18 am Màrt, VE 2,250** — *The hard winter at Tarr* (Seann Tarr). A wind out of the north holds the better part of two months without turning, and the household at Tarr lives on dried stores and shellfish taken between gales, burning at the last the timbers of a spare boat-frame kept against just such a want rather than let the hearth go cold.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0028"><em>The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3526"></a>**16 an Giblean, VE 2,250** — *The calm morning after the hard winter* (Seann Tarr). The wind drops in a single night and swings out of the north at last; the household goes down to the shingle before light to stand out of the wind, and finds a run of small fish thick enough in the shallows to be taken by hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0028"><em>The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3527"></a>**15 an Cèitean, VE 2,258** — *The four houses raised at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag* (Seann Vell). A short way above the river's mouth in the north-east, four houses and a boat-shed are raised on ground cut level into the steep bank; no dwelling of the shore-folk on the island is known to stand further to the north-east than this small place.
- <a id="ev-EI-3528"></a>**13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,260** — *A girl measures her growing by the soot* (Seann Tarr). A child of the cliff-house at Tarr stands with her back to the soot-stain on the rock above the hearth each midwinter to see how far up it her crown reaches, until the year she stands as tall as the stain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0028"><em>The cliff-house at Seann Tarr in the east</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,241</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3529"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,264** — *A flat-bottomed hull built for the river* (Seann Vell). The Vell's boat-shed is built to keep a hull dry between one season's use and the next; the household raises a boat flat enough in the bottom to be poled past the first rapids in a dry season, and takes it further upriver than any of the four households has gone on foot.
- <a id="ev-EI-3530"></a>**16 an Giblean, VE 2,270** — *A second small fire lit at the door in the dark months* (Seann Tarr). The household of the Tarr cliff-house keeps a second small fire lit just inside the door on the darkest days, more for its light than its warmth, the cliff keeping the sun from the doorway through the shortest months.
- <a id="ev-EI-3531"></a>**18 am Màrt, VE 2,290** — *A spring flood reaches the boat-shed* (Seann Vell). Snow melting fast off the central massif sends the Abhainn bheag over its bank far enough to reach the boat-shed's lower course; the household clears the silted floor by the basket-load and raises the shed a course higher on its uphill side.
- <a id="ev-EI-3532"></a>**17 an Gearran, VE 2,300** — *A girl of the river Vell stops at the river's mouth* (Seann Vell). A woman grown up at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag stands at the river's mouth one evening looking at the open sea and goes no further, holding that a river's own child has no business beyond its mouth.
- <a id="ev-EI-3533"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, VE 2,301** — *Dried fish carried south to kin without a river* (Seann Vell). The Vell on the Abhainn bheag spares a share of its eel and salmon catch, smoked over slow fires, to kin two days' walk to the south who keep no river of their own; a household comes up once in a lean year with little to trade and goes home with more than it brought.
- <a id="ev-I-0029"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,312** — *The north-eastern Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). The Seann Vell on the Abhainn bheag, a short way above its mouth in the north-east, is a small place of four houses and a boat-shed. No Seann-Dhaoine dwelling on the main island is known further to the north-east.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3527"><em>The four houses raised at the Vell on the Abhainn bheag</em>, 15 an Cèitean, VE 2,258</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3529"><em>A flat-bottomed hull built for the river</em>, 12 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,264</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3531"><em>A spring flood reaches the boat-shed</em>, 18 am Màrt, VE 2,290</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3532"><em>A girl of the river Vell stops at the river's mouth</em>, 17 an Gearran, VE 2,300</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3533"><em>Dried fish carried south to kin without a river</em>, 19 am Faoilleach, VE 2,301</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3534"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, VE 2,312** — *The eel-trap pattern taught to two children* (Seann Vell). An old woman of the Vell's youngest household teaches the willow-trap pattern she learned as a girl to a boy and a girl of the place, holding that a pattern known in only one pair of hands is one bad season from being lost to the whole Vell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0029"><em>The north-eastern Seann Vell</em>, 26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,312</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3535"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,320** — *The second Skell begins its own curved mole* (Seann Skell). A household of a northern Skell some way along the coast from the first breakwater takes up the same work for its own water, laying stone out from a low headland in the same curve, carried down from a scree behind the shore rather than quarried fresh.
- <a id="ev-EI-3536"></a>**13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,350** — *A swell breaks over the unfinished mole and moves nothing* (Seann Skell). A hard swell out of the north-west runs white over the second Skell's unfinished curve for two days; when it drops every stone is found still set where it was laid, moved a hand's width here and there but nowhere thrown clear.
- <a id="ev-EI-3537"></a>**15 an Cèitean, VE 2,360** — *Each stone of the curved mole laid dry first* (Seann Skell). The household building the second mole at the northern Skell lays each new stone dry against the course already set, working it back and forth until it sits without rocking, and only then sets it.
- <a id="ev-I-0030"></a>**22 am Màrt, VE 2,382** — *The northern Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). At the Seann Skell below the later Ros gheal, on the north coast, the Seann-Dhaoine lay a second breakwater, shorter than the southern one and curved against the swell of the open sea. The two moles are built the same way, stone by stone.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3535"><em>The second Skell begins its own curved mole</em>, 12 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,320</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3536"><em>A swell breaks over the unfinished mole and moves nothing</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,350</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3537"><em>Each stone of the curved mole laid dry first</em>, 15 an Cèitean, VE 2,360</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3538"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, VE 2,382** — *The curved mole at the second Skell finished* (Seann Skell). The second Skell's breakwater is carried out as far as the household judges worth the sheltering; a boat brought in behind the finished curve on a hard-weather day rides easier at its mooring than any boat of that shore had ridden before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0030"><em>The northern Seann Skell</em>, 22 am Màrt, VE 2,382</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3539"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, VE 2,390** — *A traveller from the second Skell sees the first mole* (Seann Skell). A man of the second Skell, grown from the boy who watched his own household's curve laid, comes within sight of the first mole on a journey south and finds the stone laid the same way, curve for curve, though no household of either shore had ever seen the other's work before it was finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0030"><em>The northern Seann Skell</em>, 22 am Màrt, VE 2,382</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3540"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, VE 2,401** — *The first clay-lined pit dug in the western dune* (Seann Vell). A woman of the western Vell digs and clay-lines the first of a line of storage pits cut into the dune's slope, closed with a heavy slab; households after her keep her spacing between pits without troubling to test her reasoning for themselves.
- <a id="ev-EI-3541"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, VE 2,418** — *A younger household cuts clay out of turn* (Seann Vell). A household new to the western dune cuts a clay bank two others had agreed to leave fallow a season; once the disagreement reaches her, the woman who keeps the unwritten turn among the banks settles it, and the younger household gives over a full pit's worth of its own dried catch.
- <a id="ev-EI-3542"></a>**16 an Lùnastal, VE 2,430** — *The pits of the western dune spaced a body's length apart* (Seann Vell). The woman who dug the first store-pit in the western dune at Vell sets her later pits a full body's length apart, holding that a pit dug too near another draws damp, and the households after her keep the spacing.
- <a id="ev-I-0031"></a>**20 an Giblean, VE 2,451** — *The western Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). At the Seann Vell of the west coast the Seann-Dhaoine dig a line of storage pits into the dune, lined with clay and lidded with slabs. Some held fish bones still when they were opened.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3540"><em>The first clay-lined pit dug in the western dune</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, VE 2,401</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3541"><em>A younger household cuts clay out of turn</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, VE 2,418</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3542"><em>The pits of the western dune spaced a body's length apart</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, VE 2,430</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3543"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, VE 2,460** — *Fish bones found in a sealed pit* (Seann Vell). A pit left sealed longer than a season gives back fish bones picked clean and gone soft with damp that found its way past the clay; the households learn to trust a pit's seal less far into a second year and to empty a store before the season turns.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0031"><em>The western Seann Vell</em>, 20 an Giblean, VE 2,451</a>.</span>

## The Years VE 2,501 – 3,000

- <a id="ev-EI-3544"></a>**6 an Gearran, VE 2,505** — *Doors of the western shore turn from the sea* (Seann Vell). Without any of its own tellings naming a reason, household after household of the western shore sets its door and its hearth a little more toward the dune at its back than toward the water in front, a threshold that had always opened straight onto the beach coming to open sideways from it instead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0031"><em>The western Seann Vell</em>, 20 an Giblean, VE 2,451</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3545"></a>**7 am Màrt, VE 2,523** — *The last pit of the season sealed for winter* (Seann Vell). The western dune's last pit of the year is dug, lined and lidded before the first hard frost, the sand banked back over its edges as every pit before it had been closed, the shore settling into a waiting none of its tellings say the whole of.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0031"><em>The western Seann Vell</em>, 20 an Giblean, VE 2,451</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3546"></a>**24 am Màrt, VE 2,524** — *The spur first climbed and looked from* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). Two sons of a shore household climb the spur above the southern lowland to look, and come back saying a man standing on its crown can see the whole lowland below him and any thing that moves across it long before it reaches the coast.
- <a id="ev-I-0032"></a>**19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524** — *Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). On a spur above the ground where Cathair mhòr now stands, the Seann-Dhaoine build the walled outpost afterwards called Làrach an Dùin-fhaire. Its stones are dressed on the outer face only, and its single gate looks inland, away from the sea.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3546"><em>The spur first climbed and looked from</em>, 24 am Màrt, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3547"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,524** — *The three rings begun on the height* (Làrach an Dùin). On a height near the south-eastern coast a crew begins the outer of three ringed walls under a woman said to read the ground before a stone is laid, a work on a scale no household of that coast has raised to before.
- <a id="ev-EI-3548"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,526** — *Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's wall dressed on its outer face only* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). The mason who sets Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's first course dresses its stone smooth only where an enemy's eye might run along it, leaving the inner face raw, so that the wall stands smooth without and rough within through every season it is kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3549"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,527** — *The inner face of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire left rough* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). The woman who sets the first course of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire wall dresses the stones on the outer face only, saying a wall need be smooth where an enemy's eye runs looking for a hold, and rough where a friend's hand rests going up the inner steps.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3550"></a>**5 an Giblean, VE 2,530** — *Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's gate hung* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). A heavy oaken gate is hung on a socketed post at Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, its single doorway facing inland away from the sea, and swings shut of its own weight for the first time to the doubt of an old fisherman who mistrusts a door built facing from the water.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3551"></a>**7 am Màrt, VE 2,531** — *Cattle first driven up the spur* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). Beasts used to level shore grazing are coaxed up the spur's steep ground for the first time, balking at the new gate, and settle within the wall to its thin grass within a few days of the climb.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3552"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,535** — *The gate argued before the lintel* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). An old fisherman argues that a gate facing away from the water is a gate built by people who have forgotten what the water was to them; the mason answers that whatever a gate here must watch for will not come rowing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3553"></a>**4 an Cèitean, VE 2,540** — *A watcher learns to prefer the quiet* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). A woman who keeps Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's first winter watch longer than anyone of her household says afterward that the quiet of the spur had a weight unlike any quiet of the shore, and that she grew almost to prefer it.
- <a id="ev-EI-3554"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,545** — *The false watch on the lowland* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). A boy of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raises the whole watch at dusk over shapes crossing the lowland from the west, taken for deer moving too evenly together; nothing is found by first light, and Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's watch is never again left to one pair of eyes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0032"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire raised</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 2,524</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3555"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, VE 2,560** — *The cistern cut into the bedrock* (Làrach an Dùin). At the height's crown a basin is hollowed from the bedrock by heated stone cracked loose and cooled with water, a labour of two seasons that blisters more hands than the rest of the rings together.
- <a id="ev-EI-3556"></a>**6 an Gearran, VE 2,570** — *The one who reads the ground stands over the cistern* (Làrach an Dùin). The woman who reads the ground for the three rings says the cistern must go deep enough to hold water through a summer no rain falls in, though no one living has seen such a summer.
- <a id="ev-I-0033"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,576** — *Làrach an Dùin raised* (Làrach an Dùin). A greater work is raised on the height near Ceann mhin: three rings of wall, a cistern cut into the bedrock, and room within, as it was later reckoned, for four hundred people and their beasts. Whether the builders of the outpost built this also has never been settled.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3547"><em>The three rings begun on the height</em>, 26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,524</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3555"><em>The cistern cut into the bedrock</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, VE 2,560</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-3556"><em>The one who reads the ground stands over the cistern</em>, 6 an Gearran, VE 2,570</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3557"></a>**8 am Faoilleach, VE 2,590** — *The cistern first full* (Làrach an Dùin). The cistern fills for the first time from a spring the digging uncovers, and a child let down on a rope draws up the first measure, which the woman who read the ground tastes and says tastes of stone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0033"><em>Làrach an Dùin raised</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,576</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3558"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, VE 2,600** — *Cattle first driven inside the three rings* (Làrach an Dùin). Beasts are driven up the steeper climb into the three rings for the first time, more lost to loose scree on the way than the spur's own herders ever lost, and a woman who loses two of her own says the rings charge dear for what they let in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0033"><em>Làrach an Dùin raised</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,576</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3559"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, VE 2,600** — *The wind within the rings* (Làrach an Dùin). A household that moves up from the shore to one of the first houses within the innermost ring finds the wind there, filtered through three walls, gentler than any wind it knew at the water's edge.
- <a id="ev-EI-3560"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, VE 2,610** — *The trodden way between the heights first paved* (Àth fhionn). A household along the worst stretch of the path between the spur and the height lays flat stones to keep its own feet dry, with no thought yet of any greater road, and others add paving of their own beside it.
- <a id="ev-EI-3561"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,622** — *The death of the woman who read the ground* (Làrach an Dùin). The woman who has read the ground for the three rings since the first course dies within the innermost ring at a great age and is buried there at her own asking, under a stretch of wall she named the soundest of her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0033"><em>Làrach an Dùin raised</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,576</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0034"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,627** — *The kerbed way between the forts* (Àth fhionn). A kerbed track, a cart's width and paved with flat slabs, is laid through the ground near Àth fhionn toward both strongholds. It is the only road the Seann-Dhaoine are known to have made away from the shore.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-3560"><em>The trodden way between the heights first paved</em>, 21 an t-Samhain, VE 2,610</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3562"></a>**18 am Faoilleach, VE 2,635** — *The kerbing of the way spreads* (Àth fhionn). Upright stones set along the paving's edges hold it firm through a wet winter better than the unkerbed stretches beside it, and the practice spreads along the whole track within a few more seasons.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0034"><em>The kerbed way between the forts</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,627</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3563"></a>**16 an Gearran, VE 2,640** — *The kerbed way paved household by household* (Àth fhionn). The track between Làrach an Dùin-fhaire and the rings is paved stretch by stretch by the households nearest each stretch, pale stone and dark, broad slabs and small fitted stones, no one hand holding the whole plan of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0034"><em>The kerbed way between the forts</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,627</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3564"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,655** — *The first cart driven the whole way* (Àth fhionn). A cart of dressed stone drawn by two yoked oxen crosses the whole kerbed way for the first time without a wheel sinking to the axle, a day's haul where the same load once took the better part of three over open moor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0034"><em>The kerbed way between the forts</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,627</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-3565"></a>**26 an Lùnastal, VE 2,678** — *The last slab of the kerbed way laid* (Àth fhionn). The final slab of the track is set tilted rather than level on the last steep rise, and the small crew that lays it turns, its work done, to look inland toward the high pale country rather than back toward the sea.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0034"><em>The kerbed way between the forts</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,627</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0035"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679** — *Làrach an Teampaill raised* (Làrach an Teampaill). A stepped platform of fitted stone is built in the eastern hills, with an altar block on its top step. The altar is set square to the central mountains. Every later temple on Dia-thìr faces some other way.
- <a id="ev-EI-4001"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, VE 2,681** — *The first steps of the platform laid* (Làrach an Teampaill). A household of the eastern hills begins laying flat stone in steps up the slope below the height, bedding each slab before the next is set above it, the first work of the platform that will in time carry the altar block on its topmost step.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4002"></a>**12 an Cèitean, VE 2,687** — *The great stone dragged up on rollers* (Làrach an Teampaill). The block meant for the platform's top step is hauled up the finished lower steps on rollers of trimmed timber, the same labour that raised Làrach an Dùin-fhaire wall and Làrach an Dùin rings, and set back from the step's outer edge to be dressed flat.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4003"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,690** — *The first dawn at the altar* (Làrach an Teampaill). A household of the southern lowland climbs the finished steps at first light on the shortest morning of the year and stands about the great stone as the sun's light runs along its face toward the mountains it is squared to. No telling records what, if anything, was said.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4004"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, VE 2,696** — *Other households begin to climb* (Làrach an Teampaill). Seeing the first household return year on year to the shortest morning, other families of the eastern hills take up the same climb, until the one gathering at the platform draws more households together than any single one of them could climb the steps alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4005"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,700** — *The shortest morning climbed in cloud* (Làrach an Teampaill). In a year when cloud lies thick over the eastern hills through the shortest morning, the households climb the platform steps in the dark and the cold all the same and stand about the great stone the whole hour the light would have taken to cross it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4006"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, VE 2,704** — *The last step laid flush with the moor* (Làrach an Teampaill). The lowest step of the platform is set flush with the level ground, closing the run years after the great stone above it already stood finished, and it is this easiest step, rather than any harder-won one above, that the households nearest it remember longest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4007"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, VE 2,706** — *A carved bird left at the stone's foot* (Làrach an Teampaill). A woman carries a small carved bird up the platform steps once and sets it at the foot of the great stone, and goes down without it; no second such bird is ever found there.
- <a id="ev-EI-4008"></a>**26 an Gearran, VE 2,711** — *A stranger turned away from the platform* (Làrach an Teampaill). A stranger up from the southern lowland asks a woman drawing water why the great stone is raised. She answers that a stone older than her grandmother's grandmother needs no explaining to one not born to it, and he does not climb the steps or come again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0035"><em>Làrach an Teampaill raised</em>, 14 an Lùnastal, VE 2,679</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4009"></a>**27 am Màrt, VE 2,717** — *The digging begins at the eastern Toll-dubh* (Toll-dubh). On level moor in the south-east a household begins cutting a well-like shaft straight down through the rock, the work continuing past any depth a well would need and its walls smoothed by hand long after the digging alone would have left them rough.
- <a id="ev-EI-4010"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,723** — *The baskets carried off and not returned* (Toll-dubh). Each evening the broken rock the digging throws off is carried away over the rise at the moor's edge, and no heap of it is ever afterward found anywhere near the shaft's mouth, though no telling says where it was taken.
- <a id="ev-I-0036"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730** — *The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east* (Toll-dubh). A shaft is sunk straight down through the rock at the eastern Toll-dubh, its walls tooled smooth as far as a lamp will show. No spoil lies beside it. Whatever was taken out was carried away, or nothing was.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4009"><em>The digging begins at the eastern Toll-dubh</em>, 27 am Màrt, VE 2,717</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4010"><em>The baskets carried off and not returned</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,723</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4011"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,731** — *A cord lengthened for the lamp* (Toll-dubh). The plaited cord that lets the lamp down to judge the smoothing of the shaft's walls is lengthened for the third time, the household gathering at the lip each time to watch the lamp go down further than it has gone before and come up still burning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4012"></a>**26 an Gearran, VE 2,735** — *A young man hurt in the eastern shaft* (Toll-dubh). Sent down to free a caught basket, a young man of the household comes up with a gash along one forearm that keeps him from the heaviest carrying a season, and returns to the cord the following spring all the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4013"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, VE 2,736** — *The cord hung inside the door* (Toll-dubh). The worn lengths of hide cord the eastern shaft was measured with are hung, when renewed, inside the household's door, where another household might hang a net.
- <a id="ev-EI-4014"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, VE 2,740** — *The lamp lowered in the eastern shaft* (Toll-dubh). The lamp is let down further than ever before, its light at the bottom showing no more of the walls than a small patch no wider than two hands held apart, the rest standing dark above and below it; the digging is remembered to have stopped near this same evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4015"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, VE 2,742** — *A stone dropped and heard to fall nowhere* (Toll-dubh). After the digging stops, a stone let fall from the lip gives back no sound of striking anything below, and the household stands listening far longer than it kept silence for anything else in all the years of that work.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4016"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, VE 2,745** — *A stone laid over the shaft at the first frost* (Toll-dubh). The household of the eastern Toll-dubh lays a flat stone loosely over the shaft's mouth at each year's first hard frost and lifts it after the shortest days, to keep a beast or a careless foot from the lip.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4017"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, VE 2,748** — *The digging begins at the western Toll-dubh* (Toll-dubh). Far across the island, on ground its own people likewise call Toll-dubh, a second household begins a straight, round shaft of the same make as the eastern one, with no telling saying that either household knew of the other's work.
- <a id="ev-EI-4018"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, VE 2,761** — *A girl asks how deep the shaft will go* (Toll-dubh). A girl of the western household asks her mother whether the shaft is being dug down to wherever the mountains keep their roots; her mother answers only that the ground keeps its own matters, and that a household does well not to ask them aloud.
- <a id="ev-EI-4019"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,765** — *An old man keeps the lamp trimmed at the western shaft* (Toll-dubh). A man of the western household, past the heaviest carrying, keeps the lamp trimmed each evening for whoever goes down to judge the smoothing of the western shaft.
- <a id="ev-EI-4020"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,770** — *The lamp left to burn itself out* (Toll-dubh). The household at the western shaft takes up a habit of setting the lamp, still burning, on a stone by the lip each evening rather than snuffing it, letting it go out on its own, a small custom none of its own tellings gives a reason for keeping.
- <a id="ev-I-0037"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,782** — *The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west* (Toll-dubh). A second shaft of the same making is cut at the western Toll-dubh, far across the island from the first. Stones thrown into either are not heard to land.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4017"><em>The digging begins at the western Toll-dubh</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, VE 2,748</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4018"><em>A girl asks how deep the shaft will go</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, VE 2,761</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4019"><em>An old man keeps the lamp trimmed at the western shaft</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,765</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4020"><em>The lamp left to burn itself out</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,770</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4021"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, VE 2,783** — *The last stone dropped at the western shaft* (Toll-dubh). On the evening the western digging is given over, the youngest of the household lets a stone fall and counts under his breath until he judges it must have struck bottom; when no sound comes, he looks to the faces around him rather than down the shaft.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0037"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,782</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4022"></a>**5 an Gearran, VE 2,795** — *The two shafts left open and shunned* (Toll-dubh). Both shafts stand unfilled and uncovered at the century's turn, and travellers of either coast come to walk wide of their mouths, letting a dropped stone go down into a silence no household troubles any longer to break by listening after it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0037"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the west</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, VE 2,782</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4023"></a>**6 am Màrt, VE 2,801** — *Bran born to the north-west shore*. Bran is born to a fishing hearth of the north-west shore, kin who keep Aithris a' Chruthachaidh as every hill hearth does but hear its westward part first, the part that names Tìr nan Òg, Magh Meall and Taigh Dhuinn across the open sea.
- <a id="ev-EI-4024"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, VE 2,815** — *Bran stands at the tideline at dusk*. Bran, near ten, is found by his mother at the tideline deep into the dark, looking at the place where it stops being water and starts being something else.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4023"><em>Bran born to the north-west shore</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 2,801</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4025"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, VE 2,825** — *The best boatman of that coast*. Grown to a man, Bran is known the length of the north-west shore as the surest hand with a swell and a stitching-needle alike, mending hulls that no other boatman's seams will hold and reading weather other men cannot.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4024"><em>Bran stands at the tideline at dusk</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, VE 2,815</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4026"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,828** — *Bran mends every boat on the shore*. Neighbours bring Bran their boats from half a day's walk along the coast because his stitches hold where other men's let the sea in, and he asks no payment but a share of what the mended boat brings home.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4025"><em>The best boatman of that coast</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 2,825</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4027"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, VE 2,829** — *Bran begins the great hull*. Bran starts gathering bull-hides cured harder and longer than any boat on his coast has needed, and sets ribs of hazel and ash closer than a hand's width, telling his kin at first only that he means a bigger boat for a bigger catch.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4026"><em>Bran mends every boat on the shore</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,828</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4028"></a>**21 an Giblean, VE 2,830** — *The great hull decked with sealed skins*. Bran decks half the length of his great hull with skins stretched and sealed against green water and sets his ribs closer than three fingers apart, and the neighbours stop believing he builds only for a bigger catch.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4027"><em>Bran begins the great hull</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 2,829</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4029"></a>**7 an Cèitean, VE 2,831** — *Bran tells his mother the boat's purpose*. Two winters into the building, Bran tells his mother plainly that he means to sail west and prove Aithris a' Chruthachaidh's word of a land beyond the sea's edge true or false. She does not forbid him, though she warns him no telling yet has anyone to bring it home.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4028"><em>The great hull decked with sealed skins</em>, 21 an Giblean, VE 2,830</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4030"></a>**20 an Cèitean, VE 2,831** — *The great hull finished*. By the second spring Bran's boat stands finished on its trestles, broader and higher at the bow than any craft that coast has built, decked with sealed skins to throw off green water, built plainly for open sea rather than the shallows.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4029"><em>Bran tells his mother the boat's purpose</em>, 7 an Cèitean, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4031"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,831** — *Blàthnaid's promise asked and given*. The night before the boat puts out, Blàthnaid asks her brother Bran to tell her the truth of whatever he finds, if ever he has the chance. He promises it, a promise she keeps for the rest of her life though he never returns to be asked again.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4030"><em>The great hull finished</em>, 20 an Cèitean, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4032"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,831** — *Bran sails west*. In high summer Bran puts out from the north-west shore with four kinsmen, holding his bow south of the grey bank that never lifts off the northern sea and west into open water no boat of that coast has crossed before. The household sends them off in silence.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4031"><em>Blàthnaid's promise asked and given</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4033"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, VE 2,831** — *Five put out west, the grey bank on the right hand*. Bran holds his bow west and a little south of the grey bank that lies on the northern sea, standing the whole first morning at the steering-oar and watching the bank fall away astern until it is nothing.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4032"><em>Bran sails west</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0038"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833** — *The First Canoe*. Among the coastal Tuathaich families a half-forgotten telling of a voyage is kept, long hushed: a steersman with a name, and a first crossing to an isle of the blessed. Their church tells it as the voyage of Naomh Breandan. The druids of the Old Faith call it idle belief.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4023"><em>Bran born to the north-west shore</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 2,801</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4025"><em>The best boatman of that coast</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 2,825</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4027"><em>Bran begins the great hull</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 2,829</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4029"><em>Bran tells his mother the boat's purpose</em>, 7 an Cèitean, VE 2,831</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4030"><em>The great hull finished</em>, 20 an Cèitean, VE 2,831</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4031"><em>Blàthnaid's promise asked and given</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,831</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4032"><em>Bran sails west</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,831</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4033"><em>Five put out west, the grey bank on the right hand</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4034"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833** — *The crewman found on the southern shingle*. A season and more after the boat put out, a woman gathering shellfish finds the youngest of the crew, Bran's sister's son, alive but near dead on a stretch of shingle two days south of his home shore, sun-blackened and too parched to speak.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4033"><em>Five put out west, the grey bank on the right hand</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4035"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833** — *The boy's telling of the green land*. Over days of broken whispers the crewman tells of many days on open water, then a green land rising from the sea where fruit hung ready and a spring broke sweet from the rock, and a welcome from a people unmarked by age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4034"><em>The crewman found on the southern shingle</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4036"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,833** — *Bran stays in the west*. The crewman tells that Bran, offered his freedom to turn home, chose to stay on the green shore, saying he would not turn from the question he had followed his whole life to answer now that his feet stood on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4035"><em>The boy's telling of the green land</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4037"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,833** — *The crewman dies*. Eleven days after he is carried in from the shingle, Bran's sister's son dies with the door left open on the sea, saying to the last that the land had not been unkind and his uncle had not looked afraid.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4036"><em>Bran stays in the west</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4038"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, VE 2,834** — *The telling spreads along the coast*. Within a year of the boy's death the telling of the green land in the west has gone the length of the north-west shore and inland besides, growing surer in each mouth than the dying boy ever claimed it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4039"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,834** — *Strangers turned from the dying boy's door*. By the fourth day after the crewman is carried in, strangers come to the door asking to see the boy who crossed the western sea, and are turned away for his quiet.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4040"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, VE 2,838** — *A boy nearly follows the telling west*. A fifteen-year-old of the shore is found in the dark sitting in a coracle he has no business taking out, looking west, and is brought home and wept over, the telling's first plain harm.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4041"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,838** — *The elders let the telling fall*. The elders of three shore households agree at a closed fire to starve the telling of the green land rather than forbid it outright, answering no stranger's question of it and teaching it to no child who has not already heard it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4042"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,840** — *Blàthnaid tells her daughter, once*. An old woman by then, Blàthnaid keeps her promise the only way left to her, telling her grown daughter the whole of the boy's account at a covered hearth, and naming her brother at the end of it: Bran.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4031"><em>Blàthnaid's promise asked and given</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,831</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4043"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, VE 2,860** — *Blàthnaid dies*. Blàthnaid dies an old woman, having told the steersman's telling to no one but her own daughter, who carries it on in the same low voice at the same covered fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4042"><em>Blàthnaid tells her daughter, once</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,840</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4044"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, VE 2,870** — *Brian digs through frozen ground for a child* (Tobar dhìreach). When a child of the black-well household dies of a fever in Brian's twentieth year, he digs through frozen ground for the better part of two days without once cursing it, and sits by the raw earth a while after.
- <a id="ev-EI-4045"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, VE 2,879** — *Brian marries Caoimhe* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian, grave-digger of the high valleys, marries Caoimhe of a herding household two valleys east, a quick-tongued woman known for setting a whole hearth laughing. Three children born to them die in their first winter, one after another.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4044"><em>Brian digs through frozen ground for a child</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, VE 2,870</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4046"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,880** — *Brian takes up the grave-digger's work* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian, of Clann a' Chlachair, becomes known through the high valleys as the one who digs the graves of the dead, a trade his father had kept before him. He is a plain, steady man, slow of speech, and the valley comes to trust his hands with its dead.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4045"><em>Brian marries Caoimhe</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, VE 2,879</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4047"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, VE 2,884** — *Brian thinks of the earth at a graveside* (Tobar dhìreach). Waiting at the edge of a fresh grave for the kin to bring the body down, Brian thinks that the dead lie still and the earth takes them, and that if the earth is to take a coal it must go deep and be left.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4046"><em>Brian takes up the grave-digger's work</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,880</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4048"></a>**24 am Màrt, VE 2,885** — *Neighbours gather to watch the coals buried* (Tobar dhìreach). Word of Brian's digging draws watchers to the graveside through the evening: an old man who had tried the coals himself in his youth, two of Sireadh's grandchildren, a boy sent home twice who comes back a third time. The talk among them does not agree.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4047"><em>Brian thinks of the earth at a graveside</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 2,884</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4049"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, VE 2,885** — *The burial words said over five coals* (Tobar dhìreach). Standing in the grave he has dug for five coals, Brian says over them the words said over every grave in the high valleys, asking the ground to hold gently what is given it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4048"><em>Neighbours gather to watch the coals buried</em>, 24 am Màrt, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0038a"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885** — *The black coal warm in the ground* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian of the Mason's line buries the five unlit coals deep in the ground beside the slab at Tobar dhìreach. When he digs them up on the next day the black coal, as black as a wet crow, is warm in his hand and smoulders as the air comes to it; the other four are as cold as the clay.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4047"><em>Brian thinks of the earth at a graveside</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 2,884</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4048"><em>Neighbours gather to watch the coals buried</em>, 24 am Màrt, VE 2,885</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4049"><em>The burial words said over five coals</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4050"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885** — *Brian reasons the earth wants its own time* (Tobar dhìreach). Standing at a fresh grave, Brian reasons that as the sea took its coal by wading and the sky by the height of a throw, the earth might take its coal only if left buried deep and undisturbed, as the dead are left. He carries the thought to Sireadh, keeper of the bag.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0027a"><em>The snowflake coal takes fire in the air</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, VE 2,170</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4049"><em>The burial words said over five coals</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4051"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,885** — *Sireadh gives Brian the five dark coals* (Tobar dhìreach). Sireadh, eldest keeper of the leather bag since Fionnghuala's day, gives Brian the five coals that have not yet answered, keeping back only her doubt that a grave-digger's guess will fare better than the trials that failed before it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4050"><em>Brian reasons the earth wants its own time</em>, 26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4052"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,885** — *The black coal set in Teine a' Chlachair* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian carries the warm black coal to the hearth at Tobar dhìreach and sets it among the embers of the fire Clann a' Chlachair holds to have burned unbroken since Oidhche an Dealanaich. It catches and burns on, and is not seen to go dark again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038a"><em>The black coal warm in the ground</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4051"><em>Sireadh gives Brian the five dark coals</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4053"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,885** — *Sireadh reads the black coal's answer* (Tobar dhìreach). Sireadh, the old widow who kept the bag sixty years, says at the graveside that the earth took the coal: the answering came at the rising out of the ground, not the lying in it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038a"><em>The black coal warm in the ground</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4051"><em>Sireadh gives Brian the five dark coals</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4054"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,886** — *Brian keeps the black coal in his own pot* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian makes a clay pot of his own, fired for the purpose, with a lid of fresh-cut turf, and keeps the black coal burning in it for the rest of his life, feeding it wood and heather and carrying it with him at his work through the high valleys.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4052"><em>The black coal set in Teine a' Chlachair</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4055"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, VE 2,895** — *Sireadh dies* (Tobar dhìreach). Sireadh dies an old woman, having lived to see the black coal warm in Brian's hand at the graveside by Leac na Fèithe.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4053"><em>Sireadh reads the black coal's answer</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4056"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,915** — *Brian teaches the grave-digger's trade* (Tobar dhìreach). Grown old, Brian gives over the heaviest digging to younger hands he has taught himself, teaching them above all to line a grave true, so the sides will not fall on what is laid in it; he goes on keeping the black coal at his own hearth.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4054"><em>Brian keeps the black coal in his own pot</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 2,886</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4057"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, VE 2,921** — *Brian dies at three-and-sixty* (Tobar dhìreach). Brian, grave-digger of the high valleys and finder of the black coal, dies at three-and-sixty, worn by his years of labour rather than by any illness the valley can name. He is buried beside Leac na Fèithe at Tobar dhìreach, near the ground he first opened for the five coals.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0038a"><em>The black coal warm in the ground</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4056"><em>Brian teaches the grave-digger's trade</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,915</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4058"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,921** — *The black coal burns at Brian's burial* (Tobar dhìreach). The pot holding the black coal is set beside Brian's grave, still burning, banked low, through the length of his burial; when the earth is given, Caoimhe lifts the pot herself and carries it home, and keeps the coal burning at her own hearth after.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4057"><em>Brian dies at three-and-sixty</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, VE 2,921</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4059"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, VE 2,921** — *The count of the coals said new at the recital* (Tobar dhìreach). At the next night of the lightning the reciter of the line adds the black coal to the count: the sea has taken the gold, the sky the white-flecked coal, and now the earth the black, gual dubh, slowly, in the dark. Four coals remain unanswered.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0038a"><em>The black coal warm in the ground</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4060"></a>**20 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,930** — *Caoimhe dies* (Tobar dhìreach). Caoimhe, wife of Brian the grave-digger, dies nine years after him, having kept the black coal burning at her own hearth all that while and never remarried; the coal passes from her hands into other keeping, banked and fed as it had been from the first.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4058"><em>The black coal burns at Brian's burial</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 2,921</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4061"></a>**20 an Giblean, VE 2,937** — *The stakes found in the tidal mud*. A boy minding his household's mooring finds a straight row of older stakes further out in the tidal mud below the north-western point, one still hung with a scrap of stitched hide. No household owns to having driven them, and who did, or from where, the mud never says.
- <a id="ev-I-0039"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,937** — *Stakes in the mud below Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). The first sure boats of the north-west coast leave their trace in the tidal mud below Ceann mhòr: a row of mooring stakes and a scrap of stitched hide. Who rowed them, and from where, is not known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4061"><em>The stakes found in the tidal mud</em>, 20 an Giblean, VE 2,937</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4501"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,940** — *The stakes shown to children with a shrug*. The line of old stakes in the mud below the north-western point comes to be called only the stakes, shown to children once by an older cousin with a shrug rather than a story.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0039"><em>Stakes in the mud below Ceann mhòr</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, VE 2,937</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4502"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,990** — *A back rises off the north-western point*. Four men working a mackerel net before dawn see a vast dark back rise smoothly from flat water off the north-west, longer than any whale known to that coast, and sink again without spray or sound. None can afterward agree how long it showed itself, only that it was greater than anything with business in water so shallow.
- <a id="ev-I-0040"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, VE 2,990** — *The Sea-Watcher first sighted* (Uilebheist na Mara). Old sailors tell of a vast creature dwelling in the waters off the north-western coast. No wreck has ever been brought up to prove them wrong.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4502"><em>A back rises off the north-western point</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 2,990</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4503"></a>**5 an Cèitean, VE 2,991** — *The sighting told at the hearths*. Within a day the four men's telling has gone the length of the coast, and within its second telling the creature has a name that will not leave it again: Uilebheist na Mara. Not every hearth believes them, but the water off the point is from that year Uilebheist na Mara's water in every mouth, believed or doubted alike.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0040"><em>The Sea-Watcher first sighted</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, VE 2,990</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4504"></a>**6 an Giblean, VE 2,995** — *The youngest of the four keeps the telling unaltered*. The youngest of the four men who saw Uilebheist na Mara rise carries the telling word for word into his old age, adding nothing and taking nothing away, and the coast counts this for more than any argument of the doubters.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0040"><em>The Sea-Watcher first sighted</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, VE 2,990</a>.</span>

## The Years VE 3,001 – 3,500

- <a id="ev-EI-4505"></a>**8 am Màrt, VE 3,015** — *Criomthann born to the shore*. Criomthann is born into a household of net-menders and boatmen kin, at some remove, to the household that once sent Bran west over the open sea. He grows up knowing the shape of that older grief by its silences rather than by being told it plainly, and it leaves him wary of open water all his life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0038"><em>The First Canoe</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, VE 2,833</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4506"></a>**7 an Gearran, VE 3,020** — *Criomthann pulls a boy from a rip*. Criomthann, still a young man, pulls a boy from a rip current with his own hand while three grown men stand arguing on the shingle about the best way to go after him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4505"><em>Criomthann born to the shore</em>, 8 am Màrt, VE 3,015</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4507"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, VE 3,035** — *Two drown in water that shows no storm*. A boat close in below the point goes over in a swell no watcher on shore can account for, and two men drown within sight of their own hearth smoke. The loss is not laid to Uilebheist na Mara, the water being the wrong water, but it teaches Criomthann, newly a father, that the sea gives little warning of the moment it means to take something.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4506"><em>Criomthann pulls a boy from a rip</em>, 7 an Gearran, VE 3,020</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4508"></a>**15 am Màrt, VE 3,042** — *Criomthann first climbs the headland with fire*. Sixteen years after the drowning below the point, Criomthann begins carrying driftwood and gorse to the last headland of that coast of an evening, less as a plan reasoned out than as a thing he finds his hands already doing, and lights a fire that will not go dark again in his lifetime.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4507"><em>Two drown in water that shows no storm</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, VE 3,035</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0041"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042** — *The beacon on the Baile chrom headland* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). A fire is kept on the headland where Taigh-solais Baile chrom now stands, and its ash lies a man's height deep. The tellings say it was lit to warn boats off the water where the Sea-Watcher was seen, and never to bring them in.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4507"><em>Two drown in water that shows no storm</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, VE 3,035</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4508"><em>Criomthann first climbs the headland with fire</em>, 15 am Màrt, VE 3,042</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4509"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, VE 3,044** — *The warning settles into few words*. Over repeated evenings calling down from the headland to boats working too far into Uilebheist na Mara's water, Criomthann's warning wears smooth into a saying his own children can say back to him in their sleep: Turn back. This water is not for you.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4508"><em>Criomthann first climbs the headland with fire</em>, 15 am Màrt, VE 3,042</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4510"></a>**7 an Gearran, VE 3,060** — *A peat bank kept for the headland fire*. Criomthann's household keeps aside a bank of peat cut for the headland fire alone, touched for nothing else, so that the fire is never let go dark even in the leanest winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4509"><em>The warning settles into few words</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, VE 3,044</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4511"></a>**8 am Màrt, VE 3,070** — *Criomthann's wife dies of a fever*. A fever that takes half the young children of the north-western shore in one bad season takes Criomthann's wife with them, and he keeps the headland fire nine years a widower.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4510"><em>A peat bank kept for the headland fire</em>, 7 an Gearran, VE 3,060</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4512"></a>**6 an Giblean, VE 3,078** — *Criomthann's strength fails the climb*. Nine years widowed, at three-and-sixty Criomthann can no longer carry wood up the last steep pitch of the headland, and his eldest son takes up the feeding of the fire, so that the flame he lit for no reason he could fully name burns on past the reach of his own life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4511"><em>Criomthann's wife dies of a fever</em>, 8 am Màrt, VE 3,070</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4513"></a>**5 an Cèitean, VE 3,079** — *Criomthann dies*. Criomthann dies at four-and-sixty in his own bed, three generations of his kin about him, having outlived every one of the four who first saw Uilebheist na Mara rise. At his own asking he is buried on the lower slope of the headland, within sound of the fire he kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4512"><em>Criomthann's strength fails the climb</em>, 6 an Giblean, VE 3,078</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4514"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, VE 3,090** — *A calm summer fills the nets at Ros ruadh* (Ros ruadh). A run of flat, windless weather settles over the water off Ros ruadh, the kind of calm fishermen pray for and seldom get, and the settlement's boats work it harder than any season in memory.
- <a id="ev-EI-4515"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, VE 3,090** — *The first boat fails to come home* (Ros ruadh). A boat with three men aboard, working water well inside what the settlement calls safe, does not return with the tide. No wreckage of it is ever found on any shingle the length of that coast.
- <a id="ev-EI-4516"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,093** — *The second boat fails eleven days after the first* (Ros ruadh). A second boat of Ros ruadh, with two men aboard, fails to come home eleven days after the first, from a different stretch of the same calm water, and again no wreckage is found.
- <a id="ev-EI-4517"></a>**24 an t-Sultain, VE 3,094** — *Seven boats lost from Ros ruadh in one season* (Ros ruadh). Boat after boat fails to return through a summer of unbroken calm, until seven are lost from Ros ruadh with no storm to blame and no wreck or body ever recovered. Scarcely a hearth in the settlement is left untouched.
- <a id="ev-I-0042"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, VE 3,094** — *Seven boats lost off Ros ruadh* (Ros ruadh). Seven boats are lost from Ros ruadh in one calm season, with no storm to blame.
