It is the first loss laid at the door of the Sea-Watcher by name; before this it was feared only in general.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4514"><em>A calm summer fills the nets at Ros ruadh</em>, 14 an Dàmhair, VE 3,090</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4515"><em>The first boat fails to come home</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, VE 3,090</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4516"><em>The second boat fails eleven days after the first</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,093</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4517"><em>Seven boats lost from Ros ruadh in one season</em>, 24 an t-Sultain, VE 3,094</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4518"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,095** — *The widows name Uilebheist na Mara* (Ros ruadh). The widows of Ros ruadh are the first to say plainly, at every hearth that will hear it, that Uilebheist na Mara has taken their seven boats. It is the first loss on that coast laid at Uilebheist na Mara's door by name rather than only feared in its shadow, and the naming holds ever after.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-I-0042"><em>Seven boats lost off Ros ruadh</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 3,094</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4519"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,096** — *Kin from three households feed the beacon together*. In the year after the widows' naming, the headland fire burns harder than in any year since Criomthann first lit it, fed now by hands from three households besides his own grandson's, as though a fire fed by more hands might answer for what seamanship could not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4520"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,120** — *The ash on the headland stands a man's height deep*. Fed and banked and fed again by hands born after the worst of the lost season, the beacon's ash has by now been heaped on the same ground for so many lifetimes that it stands a man's own height deep, deep enough that a boy sent to feed it can stand in the hollow of it and be seen from below only from the shoulders up.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0041"><em>The beacon on the Baile chrom headland</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,042</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4521"></a>**24 an Cèitean, VE 3,146** — *Seven empty places on the shingle* (Ros ruadh). The shingle at Ros ruadh has by now shifted through enough winters' tides that it no longer holds even the memory of where the seven lost boats once lay drawn up among the rest, and only the headland fire and the widows' naming remain to say the seven ever went out from that shore at all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0042"><em>Seven boats lost off Ros ruadh</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 3,094</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0043"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, VE 3,147** — *The seal hunt moves south* (Caol mhòr). The hunters of the north-west leave the open water and work the southern side of the headlands, out of the Sea-Watcher's sight. The seal bones thin in the middens of the north-west and grow at Caol mhòr and Cuan bheag.
- <a id="ev-EI-4522"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, VE 3,150** — *The open-water hunt gives way to the strait* (Bothan a' Chaolais). Crew by crew, the boats of the north-west leave the open coast off the last headland for the sheltered water in its lee, keeping the whole of their ground in sight at once. The seal grounds at Ros ruadh and the outer skerries thin as the strait grounds fill.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0043"><em>The seal hunt moves south</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, VE 3,147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4523"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,155** — *An old steersman says the island's hand has drawn back* (Bothan a' Chaolais). An old steersman of the strait says, at a gathering for net-mending, that the sea has not grown smaller, only that the island's hand has drawn back from the part of it a man can no longer trust.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0043"><em>The seal hunt moves south</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, VE 3,147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4524"></a>**26 an Gearran, VE 3,160** — *The middens of Bothan a' Chaolais outgrow the old grounds* (Bothan a' Chaolais). Shell and bone rise faster at Bothan a' Chaolais than they have ever risen, until the bothy folk say a winter's leavings there would wall a house. An old steersman of the strait says plainly what the coast has already done without saying it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0043"><em>The seal hunt moves south</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, VE 3,147</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4525"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, VE 3,180** — *Eimhir born to a herding household of Doire uaine* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Eimhir is born into a herding family of the high pastures south of Tobar dhìreach, in country the hill folk still call the green grove for the oaks it once bore. She grows to the flock and the ground before she grows to much else.
- <a id="ev-I-0044"></a>**8 an Cèitean, VE 3,199** — *Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills* (Doire uaine). Inscriptions are cut on rock faces all across the Doire uaine hills, more than anywhere else on the island, in lines that run for yards. Some lines are cut over and defaced with the same kind of tool that made them.
- <a id="ev-EI-4526"></a>**25 an Giblean, VE 3,200** — *A ewe strays into a defile of the hills* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). A ewe strays in the night up a narrow defile of the Doire uaine hills where the flock is not taken, and Eimhir follows it before first light into a fold of the hill she does not remember walking.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0044"><em>Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 8 an Cèitean, VE 3,199</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4525"><em>Eimhir born to a herding household of Doire uaine</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, VE 3,180</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4527"></a>**9 an Gearran, VE 3,210** — *Eimhir finds the cut stone* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Following a strayed ewe up an unfamiliar defile before dawn, Eimhir comes on a rock face cut with lines of writing no hand of that country claims, running the height of the stone and further, in a hand unlike any boundary-mark or tally she knows.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0044"><em>Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 8 an Cèitean, VE 3,199</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4526"><em>A ewe strays into a defile of the hills</em>, 25 an Giblean, VE 3,200</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4528"></a>**27 am Màrt, VE 3,210** — *Elders of the hills judge the writing older than living memory* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). A small company of the hill country's elders climbs to see the cut stone for itself. One tests it with a flat palm and says nothing; another, walking its length twice, says she knows no hand that claims the writing, and holds that the country will come to know it in its own time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0044"><em>Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 8 an Cèitean, VE 3,199</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4527"><em>Eimhir finds the cut stone</em>, 9 an Gearran, VE 3,210</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4529"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, VE 3,212** — *The hills come to a common telling of the writing* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Within two winters, gathered out of dreams two or three swear separately to the same shape and out of half-kept scraps no one can trace to a source, every hearth of that country can tell what the cutting is held to say: a thing that does not breathe, and falls on any fire it sees lit.
- <a id="ev-EI-4530"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,212** — *Dreams of the same shape at several hearths* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Two or three people of the Doire uaine hills swear, without having spoken to one another, that they have dreamed in nearly the same shape of something walking the ridges without breath.
- <a id="ev-EI-4531"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, VE 3,213** — *The second cutting is argued over at the hearths* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). That parts of the writing were struck across afterward, by what seems the very tool that first cut them, divides the hill country's telling: some hold the writer came back to unwrite a part too dangerous to keep whole; others hold the thing named in the writing did the defacing itself.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4528"><em>Elders of the hills judge the writing older than living memory</em>, 27 am Màrt, VE 3,210</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4532"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, VE 3,215** — *Children go less often alone to the far pastures* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Without any rule said aloud, fewer households of the Doire uaine hills send a child alone to the farthest grazing after the finding of the writing, and fewer let a night fire burn low and unwatched when the wind comes strange off the high ground.
- <a id="ev-EI-4533"></a>**25 an Giblean, VE 3,230** — *Two herders see the walker on the ridge and live* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Caught by dusk driving beasts home, two herders of the hills see an upright figure walk the crest against the last light, breathing no cloud into the cold air. Neither has a fire lit or a light shown on the path, and both come home to tell it.
- <a id="ev-EI-4534"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,230** — *The defile given a wide berth* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). By common unspoken consent the defile where the cut stone stands is given a wide berth, and a strayed sheep is fetched from it only by daylight and never by a child alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0044"><em>Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 8 an Cèitean, VE 3,199</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4535"></a>**24 an Cèitean, VE 3,250** — *Eimhir teaches her children the fire and the ridge* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Eimhir teaches her children that the writing is there, that no one reads it, and that a fire built where the ridge can see it is a fire built carelessly, whatever else a person believes.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4531"><em>The second cutting is argued over at the hearths</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, VE 3,213</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0045"></a>**9 an Giblean, VE 3,251** — *The Hollow Man of Doire uaine* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). The inscriptions of the Doire uaine hills tell of something that walked without breathing, and fell upon any who lit a fire in its sight.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4529"><em>The hills come to a common telling of the writing</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, VE 3,212</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4530"><em>Dreams of the same shape at several hearths</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,212</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4531"><em>The second cutting is argued over at the hearths</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, VE 3,213</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4533"><em>Two herders see the walker on the ridge and live</em>, 25 an Giblean, VE 3,230</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4535"><em>Eimhir teaches her children the fire and the ridge</em>, 24 an Cèitean, VE 3,250</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4536"></a>**26 an Gearran, VE 3,260** — *The first hearth is dug and roofed at Doire uaine* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). A household newly come to the eastern side of the hills digs its cooking fire into a pit and roofs it with a slab, showing no flame above ground. Mocked at first, the family's fire burns unremarked through a hard winter, and two more households follow within the year.
- <a id="ev-EI-4537"></a>**27 am Màrt, VE 3,261** — *Eimhir keeps her hearth open against the new custom* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). With half the hearths of the hill country dug in or talking of it, Eimhir, old now, tells her daughter she will not hide the fire her family has always kept open to the sky, having touched the writing on the stone herself before any household thought to cover its light.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4535"><em>Eimhir teaches her children the fire and the ridge</em>, 24 an Cèitean, VE 3,250</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4538"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, VE 3,262** — *Eimhir dies* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Eimhir dies of no illness the hill country can name, worn out by a long life, and is buried above her family's grazing with a stone set on end and no other marker. Her daughter banks her hearth for the last time and does not build it open again.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4537"><em>Eimhir keeps her hearth open against the new custom</em>, 27 am Màrt, VE 3,261</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4539"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, VE 3,300** — *The covered hearth spreads short of a rule* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Within forty years an open fire on the bare floor grows rare enough in the Doire uaine hills that a child raised to one is asked after it at every gathering, though households on the country's quieter edges still keep the old way, and no rule yet binds the rest.
- <a id="ev-EI-4540"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,304** — *Laoghaire begins the first pit-hearth* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). On a shoulder of ground below his own house, Laoghaire digs a hearth a man's height into the earth, with a blind angled shaft down to it and a slab dragged over the top, and sleeps beside it the first night to learn whether it holds its heat and shows no light above.
- <a id="ev-I-0046"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304** — *The hill fires go under the ground* (Doire uaine). After the inscriptions the hearths of the Doire uaine hills are dug into pits and roofed with slabs. No open hearth shows in those hills for many lifetimes. The people stay, and hide their light.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4536"><em>The first hearth is dug and roofed at Doire uaine</em>, 26 an Gearran, VE 3,260</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EI-4537"><em>Eimhir keeps her hearth open against the new custom</em>, 27 am Màrt, VE 3,261</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-4539"><em>The covered hearth spreads short of a rule</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 3,300</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-4540"><em>Laoghaire begins the first pit-hearth</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4541"></a>**22 an Lùnastal, VE 3,304** — *The blind bend in the shaft* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Laoghaire cuts the way down to his pit-hearth as a slanting shaft bent near its foot, so that no glow from below can climb it straight, and leads the smoke out through a crack in the turf ten paces off.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4540"><em>Laoghaire begins the first pit-hearth</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4542"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, VE 3,304** — *Laoghaire sleeps the first night in the pit* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Laoghaire sleeps the first night the pit-hearth is whole beside its fire under Leac na Fèithe, listening for anything on the turf above, and comes up at first light with soot on his hands and nothing heard.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4541"><em>The blind bend in the shaft</em>, 22 an Lùnastal, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4543"></a>**7 an Giblean, VE 3,305** — *Two more households dig the like* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Within the season two households of Laoghaire's own kin dig covered hearths beside their own doors on the pattern he showed them, the first word of the pit under Leac na Fèithe carried hearth to hearth the way any useful thing travelled in those hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4542"><em>Laoghaire sleeps the first night in the pit</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4544"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, VE 3,308** — *The line at Tobar dhìreach is asked to cover its fire*. Kin by marriage from the Doire uaine households ask outright at Tobar dhìreach why the household of the mason's own fire alone keeps an open hearth. The keeper of the pot answers that a fire never once let go dark cannot now be hidden without being treated as any lesser fire, and the line's hearth stays open.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4545"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, VE 3,310** — *The line keeps its hearth open* (Tobar dhìreach). The man who keeps the pot at Tobar dhìreach answers every neighbour who asks why the line will not cover its fire that Teine a' Chlachair is owed better than to be hidden as a hillside peat-fire hides from its fears.
- <a id="ev-EI-4546"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, VE 3,320** — *The custom spreads through the hills* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Within a handful of years it is the open hearth that wants explaining and the covered one that needs none; households across the Doire uaine hills dig their own, some by Laoghaire's own hand, until no open hearth shows in that country any longer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4543"><em>Two more households dig the like</em>, 7 an Giblean, VE 3,305</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4547"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, VE 3,325** — *A branch at Tobar dhìreach digs a hearth apart*. One branch of Clann a' Chlachair digs itself a covered hearth away from the line's own house, keeping the open fire only for the recital nights. The compromise satisfies no one fully and is quietly let drop again within two generations.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4548"></a>**20 an Gearran, VE 3,330** — *Laoghaire digs for a widowed sister* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Laoghaire digs three more pit-hearths in his life, one for a widowed sister and two for households that beg it of him, for he alone seems to hold in his head how far the blind bend must run.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4546"><em>The custom spreads through the hills</em>, 30 an Lùnastal, VE 3,320</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4549"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, VE 3,341** — *Laoghaire dies* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). Laoghaire dies at six-and-sixty in his own house, having outlived two of his own children and dug covered hearths for kin across the hills. He is buried on the shoulder of ground above the pit he dug first, which his sons keep in use for three generations after him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-4548"><em>Laoghaire digs for a widowed sister</em>, 20 an Gearran, VE 3,330</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0047"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,351** — *The nine at the hill camp* (Muileann chiar). Nine people die inside a hut at the camp where Muileann chiar was afterwards built, and lie where they fell beside a hearth of fresh ash. No wound is found on any bone. The hut is never opened again, and none is buried from it.
- <a id="ev-EI-4550"></a>**10 am Faoilleach, VE 3,352** — *The hill camp found silent* (Muileann chiar). A shepherd going up to a wintering camp in the south of the massif, seeing no smoke rise from it, finds a hut's door standing open and nine people within lying dead beside a cold hearth, unmarked by wound or struggle. None who come after will go in to bury them.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0047"><em>The nine at the hill camp</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,351</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4551"></a>**8 an Gearran, VE 3,352** — *The camp is left for good* (Muileann chiar). The hut with the nine dead in it is left standing, its door swinging, until the wattle rots and the roof falls over them. Other households drive their beasts wide of that shoulder of hill from that season on, and none resettles the camp.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0047"><em>The nine at the hill camp</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,351</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4552"></a>**9 am Màrt, VE 3,379** — *A family new to the hills builds an open hearth*. Kin from the eastern farms, new to grazing left unclaimed since the camp was given up, build their first house on the old pattern with the hearth open to the roof-hole, hearing the custom of the covered hearth only as a traveller's tale and keeping their fire open through their first autumn despite their neighbours' warning.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4553"></a>**7 an Giblean, VE 3,380** — *The empty house with the fire still burning*. A boy sent at dawn to borrow fire finds the new household's door standing open, the beds thrown back, and every soul of the house gone without blood, struggle or track in the fresh snow. The banked hearth burns on into the empty room exactly as it was left the night before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4554"></a>**6 an Cèitean, VE 3,395** — *An old woman warns the newcomers twice*. An old woman of the next valley walks up twice in a summer to tell a family new to the hills that a people does not dig into its own ground for a hundred years over nothing; they thank her and keep their fire open.
- <a id="ev-EI-4555"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,400** — *Two herders see the walker on the ridge* (Muileann chiar). A man and his sister-in-law, out after strayed ewes above the old camp in failing light, see a shape walk the skyline like a man and give off no breath into the cold air. They neither call out nor light a fire near them that evening, and come home unharmed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0045"><em>The Hollow Man of Doire uaine</em>, 9 an Giblean, VE 3,251</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-4556"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,407** — *The covered hearth becomes the hills' law* (Na Teallaichean Falaichte). By the year the two herders come down off the ridge, the pit under Leac na Fèithe is no longer a new thing spreading household by household but simply how a hearth is built in that country; a child born there that year will grow old without ever seeing an open fire under any roof but the one at Tobar dhìreach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0046"><em>The hill fires go under the ground</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0048"></a>**21 an Giblean, VE 3,408** — *Coille Naomh Muileann chiar set aside* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). A forest is held sacred long before any order of the Old Faith claims it. The trees knew it first, the old telling says, and the people after.
- <a id="ev-EI-5001"></a>**2 an Giblean, VE 3,420** — *The wood-carriers go the long way round* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Households whose fields run up to Coille Naomh Muileann chiar carry their winter fuel from beyond the far shoulder of open ground, two journeys where one would serve, sooner than put an axe within the wood's bounds.
- <a id="ev-I-0049"></a>**23 am Màrt, VE 3,470** — *No axe in the grove* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). The families at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar carry their fuel a half-day's walk sooner than cut a branch within it. The charcoal in their hearths is of every wood but that one.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5001"><em>The wood-carriers go the long way round</em>, 2 an Giblean, VE 3,420</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5002"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,480** — *An uncle grumbles at the wood-carriers' long way round* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). At the end of a hard winter month, one of Sadhbh's uncles says aloud, half in jest, that a tree is a tree wherever it grows and a fire does not ask where its wood was cut. No one answers him, and by the next carrying he goes the long way round with the rest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0049"><em>No axe in the grove</em>, 23 am Màrt, VE 3,470</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5003"></a>**30 an Cèitean, VE 3,496** — *Sadhbh asks what comes of a man who cuts there* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Sadhbh as a child asks her father what would come of a man who cut in Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and is told that no one has ever found out and that he has no wish to be the first.

## The Years VE 3,501 – 4,000

- <a id="ev-I-0050"></a>**11 am Màrt, VE 3,513** — *The white stag of the grove* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Three hunters see a white stag at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and none of them draws. This is the first telling of it. The stag returns in the tellings again and again; in this age it has no god.
- <a id="ev-EI-5004"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, VE 3,518** — *Sadhbh and two others meet the white stag* (Gleann nan Damh). At the narrow turn of Gleann nan Damh, a white stag breaks from the treeline of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar rather than the open hill. Sadhbh, her cousin Oscar and a boy new to the drive all have clean sight of it and time to loose, and none of the three draws.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0050"><em>The white stag of the grove</em>, 11 am Màrt, VE 3,513</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5003"><em>Sadhbh asks what comes of a man who cuts there</em>, 30 an Cèitean, VE 3,496</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5005"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,519** — *The tale of the stag goes hearth to hearth* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). The telling of the white stag passes from the nearest hearth outward, gathering colour but losing none of its bones. Some elders say the wood itself put the beast out to be seen; no one that first year gives it a name, god or otherwise.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0050"><em>The white stag of the grove</em>, 11 am Màrt, VE 3,513</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5004"><em>Sadhbh and two others meet the white stag</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, VE 3,518</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5006"></a>**4 am Màrt, VE 3,521** — *Hunters begin letting the gully's beasts go rather than risk the wrong one* (Gleann nan Damh). Carrying the tale of the stag with them, hunters at the glen let a drive go free more readily whenever it breaks for the treeline, at a real cost in meat foregone, rather than risk striking a beast they should not have struck.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0050"><em>The white stag of the grove</em>, 11 am Màrt, VE 3,513</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5007"></a>**3 an Gearran, VE 3,530** — *The white stag is seen again* (Gleann nan Damh). Twenty-two years after Sadhbh's own meeting, a fresh pair of hunters born after the first seeing find a white stag standing at the same treeline. It is taken for the same beast, or near enough that none troubles to argue the difference, and from this second seeing the tale becomes the whole country's, not one hunter's alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0050"><em>The white stag of the grove</em>, 11 am Màrt, VE 3,513</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5008"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, VE 3,566** — *Sadhbh dies* (Gleann nan Damh). Sadhbh, hunter of the eastern households and one of the three who once let the white stag go unloosed at the glen's turn, dies an old woman, having spent her last years telling the tale at hearths that were not her own and refusing, each time she was asked, to make one cause of the stag's wood and the wood of the stones.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0050"><em>The white stag of the grove</em>, 11 am Màrt, VE 3,513</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5005"><em>The tale of the stag goes hearth to hearth</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,519</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0051"></a>**9 an Giblean, VE 3,570** — *Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag left unclaimed* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). A second forest, that seems older than the first, is never settled, never felled, and never walked from end to end.
- <a id="ev-EI-5009"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, VE 3,575** — *Three paths end at the same line of stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). The three paths that run toward the second wood from three quarters are all found, without any household having agreed it, to stop at the same low line of set stones short of the trees.
- <a id="ev-EI-5010"></a>**16 an Cèitean, VE 3,600** — *Children are taught the rule of the stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Households near the second wood teach their children early and plainly to go as far as the low line of set stones and no further, and to let go whatever strays past it, for nothing lost beyond the line has ever been recovered.
- <a id="ev-EI-5011"></a>**14 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,610** — *Children told to let a lost thing go past the stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Children of the country of the second wood are told early and plainly: go as far as the stones and no further, and whatever crosses the line ahead of you, a ball or a lamb or a hound, let it go.
- <a id="ev-I-0052"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618** — *The paths that stop at a line of stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Tracks are worn toward Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag from three quarters, and all three end at a low line of set stones some way short of the trees. Beyond the stones the ground is not worn.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5009"><em>Three paths end at the same line of stones</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, VE 3,575</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5010"><em>Children are taught the rule of the stones</em>, 16 an Cèitean, VE 3,600</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5012"></a>**19 am Màrt, VE 3,620** — *Muireall crosses the line of stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Left watching for evening deer with other children at the line of set stones before Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the nine-year-old Muireall passes into the trees unseen and uncalled. The eldest child, turned away only a moment, finds her gone with no cry and no mark but a small gap in the undergrowth.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5013"></a>**17 an Giblean, VE 3,620** — *The whole country comes up with torches* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Every household within half a day's walk comes with torches cut and lit before full dark, calling Muireall's name in a chorus that carries over the still evening. They reach the line of stones together and stop there; no torch and no foot crosses it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5012"><em>Muireall crosses the line of stones</em>, 19 am Màrt, VE 3,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5014"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, VE 3,620** — *Muireall's mother asks the wood to give the child back* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). Held at the stones by her own kin, Muireall's mother asks the wood once, low enough that only those nearest her hear it, to return the child. No answer comes but the ordinary movement of leaves any wood gives back to any question.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5013"><em>The whole country comes up with torches</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 3,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5015"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, VE 3,620** — *The search narrows and ends at the stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). For three days the country works every fold of ground on the near side of the line and finds no print, no scrap of wool, no trace of Muireall's voice on any wind. On the third day the search stops at the stones, not for want of looking, but because there is nowhere left to look that does not mean crossing a line no one in living memory has ever crossed and returned across.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5014"><em>Muireall's mother asks the wood to give the child back</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, VE 3,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5016"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,621** — *The hearths say the sìth took the child* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). With nothing found on the near side of the stones, the hearths give the plainest telling that fits: that the sìth, the people of the hills and mounds who held that country first, took Muireall across the line she crossed, and that no household has yet gone in after anything lost that way and come back the better.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5015"><em>The search narrows and ends at the stones</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 3,620</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5017"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, VE 3,621** — *Muireall's household sets a stone by its own threshold*. With no body to bury, Muireall's household cuts her name into a stone of their own setting near their own door rather than at the wood, so that whoever asks after it is told of a child lost at a line of stones on a fine summer evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5016"><em>The hearths say the sìth took the child</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,621</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5018"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, VE 3,630** — *A grown hand kept near the children at the stones* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). After Muireall is lost no household lets its children watch for deer at that stretch of the line of stones without a grown hand near enough to close on a small arm.
- <a id="ev-EI-5019"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, VE 3,639** — *The rule of the stones becomes unquestioned custom* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). A generation on from Muireall's loss, no household near the second wood lets its children watch for deer at the line without a grown hand near enough to hold them back, and children born since grow up knowing the rule before they ever hear the reason for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052"><em>The paths that stop at a line of stones</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 3,618</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5020"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, VE 3,640** — *Cormac born to the keeper's hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac is born the eleventh child and fourth son of the household that keeps the bag of dark coals and the recital at Tobar dhìreach, one child among many and not looked to for the line.
- <a id="ev-EI-5021"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, VE 3,655** — *The keeping falls to Cormac* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac's two elder brothers die within one season, one of a fever and one of a fall on the scree above the black well, and the bag of four dark coals and the recital pass to Cormac on his father's death soon after.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5020"><em>Cormac born to the keeper's hearth</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, VE 3,640</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5022"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, VE 3,655** — *Cormac's brothers die in one season* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac's two elder brothers die within a season of each other in his fifteenth year, one of a fever and one of a fall on the scree above the black well, and the learning of the recital comes to him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5021"><em>The keeping falls to Cormac</em>, 26 an t-Sultain, VE 3,655</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5023"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, VE 3,660** — *Cormac marries Aoibheann* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac takes Aoibheann of a herding household two valleys west, who keeps his hearth and, as they grow old together, his fire-pot and his temper both.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5022"><em>Cormac's brothers die in one season</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 3,655</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5024"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,662** — *The red-brown coal buried a second time* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac digs a second, deeper hole beside Leac na Fèithe and lays the red-brown coal in it, thinking the earth wants more time than it gave Brian; it lies as cold as before.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0038a"><em>The black coal warm in the ground</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, VE 2,885</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5023"><em>Cormac marries Aoibheann</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, VE 3,660</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5025"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,665** — *Gual airgid carried to three rivers* (Tobar dhìreach). In one summer Cormac carries gual airgid to three different rivers of the high valleys in turn, in case the Abhainn ghorm alone had been asked; each returns it dark.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5024"><em>The red-brown coal buried a second time</em>, 30 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,662</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5026"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,669** — *Cormac thinks the grove may hold a leaving* (Tobar dhìreach). Through a wet spring while the lambs are born Cormac turns over the thought that the grove where Coimhdeach na Fine stood may hold some leaving that would answer a coal as the ground at Tobar dhìreach answered Brian.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5025"><em>Gual airgid carried to three rivers</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,665</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5027"></a>**10 am Màrt, VE 3,670** — *Cormac resolves on the grove* (Tobar dhìreach). Turning the failed trials over through a wet spring, Cormac comes to think that the grove where Coimhdeach na Fine once stood may hold in its ground some leaving that would answer a coal, and tells Aoibheann he means to carry the four dark coals north to it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5026"><em>Cormac thinks the grove may hold a leaving</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,669</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5028"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,670** — *The maul turns on the red-brown coal* (Doire ghlas). On the last morning of his month under the oaks Cormac sets the red-brown coal on a flat stone to break it open, and the maul turns on its hard curved face and comes down across the back of his left hand.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5027"><em>Cormac resolves on the grove</em>, 10 am Màrt, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0052a"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670** — *The blood of the misstrike* (Doire ghlas). Cormac of the Mason's line carries the four unlit coals to the grove at Doire ghlas, where the Keeper first spoke, and sets about breaking them there. His hammer misses and opens the back of his hand, and where the blood falls on the red-brown coal it takes fire. The kindred call it the coal of life.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5027"><em>Cormac resolves on the grove</em>, 10 am Màrt, VE 3,670</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5028"><em>The maul turns on the red-brown coal</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5029"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670** — *Cormac sets out for Doire ghlas* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac walks north from Tobar dhìreach with the four dark coals in a leather bag, oatcake and dried mutton over his other shoulder, and no company, reaching the oaks of Doire ghlas on the evening of the third day.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0011a"><em>The Keeper in the grove</em>, 17 an Gearran, VE 890</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5028"><em>The maul turns on the red-brown coal</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5030"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670** — *A month under the oaks* (Doire ghlas). Cormac keeps a small fire in the lee of a fallen trunk at Doire ghlas for the better part of a month, laying each dark coal in turn at the foot of every old oak he finds, burying them again, and once speaking to the grove outright; nothing answers him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5029"><em>Cormac sets out for Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5031"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670** — *The blood of the misstrike* (Doire ghlas). In a temper at the month's end Cormac sets the red-brown coal on a stone to break it open; the hammer turns on the hard surface and lays open the back of his other hand, and where his blood falls on the coal it catches, burning quietly the colour of firelight through oak while he kneels the better part of a day and forgets to bind the wound.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0052a"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5030"><em>A month under the oaks</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5032"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670** — *Cormac breaks camp* (Doire ghlas). With his hand bound and the coal of life gone quiet again, Cormac leaves Doire ghlas the same afternoon, judging that the grove itself had answered nothing and the finding had come out of his own blood and not the wood.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5031"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5033"></a>**6 an Gearran, VE 3,671** — *Cormac's return* (Tobar dhìreach). Four days on the road with his wound slowing him, Cormac comes down into the high valleys at evening; Aoibheann, who has watched the northern track for a week, meets him running in the yard, and hears the whole of it before he will go in to the fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052a"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5032"><em>Cormac breaks camp</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,670</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5034"></a>**7 am Màrt, VE 3,671** — *The byname of the Misstrike* (Tobar dhìreach). The valley, which had long since stopped laughing at anything Clann a' Chlachair brought home from the grove, takes to calling Cormac by his scarred hand, Cormac of the Misstrike, and he wears the name and the scar both without complaint.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5033"><em>Cormac's return</em>, 6 an Gearran, VE 3,671</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5035"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, VE 3,671** — *Cormac holds up his scarred hand at the recital* (Tobar dhìreach). At the next night of the lightning Cormac stands at the hearth with his scarred hand raised for the valley to see and speaks the new line: a fourth coal has answered, quick, out of a man's own blood.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052a"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5034"><em>The byname of the Misstrike</em>, 7 am Màrt, VE 3,671</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5036"></a>**5 an Giblean, VE 3,672** — *The fourth coal named at the recital* (Tobar dhìreach). At the next telling of the Line on Oidhche an Dealanaich, Cormac holds up his scarred hand before the gathered valley and speaks the new line into the recital: the sea, the sky and the earth had answered, and now a fourth had answered out of a man's own blood, called gual donn-ruadh and, oftener, the coal of life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0052a"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5035"><em>Cormac holds up his scarred hand at the recital</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, VE 3,671</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5037"></a>**4 an Cèitean, VE 3,690** — *A cousin tries the silver again* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac gives gual airgid over to a younger cousin to carry to the rivers in his stead, and lives to see that trial fail as his own had, and to laugh about it with Aoibheann.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5036"><em>The fourth coal named at the recital</em>, 5 an Giblean, VE 3,672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5038"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, VE 3,700** — *Children shown the old scar in the firelight* (Tobar dhìreach). For some years children of the high valleys are shown the scar on old Cormac's hand in the firelight and told the coal that would not break and the blood that lit it anyway.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5037"><em>A cousin tries the silver again</em>, 4 an Cèitean, VE 3,690</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5039"></a>**18 an Gearran, VE 3,712** — *Cormac dies at his own hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Cormac dies in his two-and-seventieth year at Tobar dhìreach, Poit an Teine burning near him as it burned near every keeper before him, his last clear word a complaint of the old scar aching in the damp.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0052a"><em>The blood of the misstrike</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, VE 3,670</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5038"><em>Children shown the old scar in the firelight</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 3,700</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5040"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,712** — *The bag passes on unnamed* (Tobar dhìreach). The leather bag with gual airgid, the coal that has never yet been tried by fire, and gual bogha-froise passes from Cormac's grave to a younger kinsman of the line, whose name the recital keeps but does not give to strangers.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5039"><em>Cormac dies at his own hearth</em>, 18 an Gearran, VE 3,712</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5041"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, VE 3,718** — *Aoibheann's last years* (Tobar dhìreach). Aoibheann outlives Cormac by six years at Tobar dhìreach, and it is from her telling, repeated at the hearth, that the valley's children learn the story of the coal that would not break and the blood that lit it anyway.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5039"><em>Cormac dies at his own hearth</em>, 18 an Gearran, VE 3,712</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0053"></a>**10 an Gearran, VE 3,720** — *The deer-drives of the eastern forest* (Doire fhionn). Lines of stakes and brush are set to drive the red deer of the eastern woods into a gully near Doire fhionn, where they are killed with spears. The antlers of the greatest stags are stacked apart from the rest.
- <a id="ev-EI-5042"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,720** — *Dubhghall drives the gully alone for the first time* (Gleann nan Damh). At twenty-five, Dubhghall stands for the first time at the head of the deer-drive he has watched his uncle lead since boyhood, and takes a stag with a bad throw that his uncle and two others must finish for him, a failure the household forgets within the season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0053"><em>The deer-drives of the eastern forest</em>, 10 an Gearran, VE 3,720</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5043"></a>**8 am Faoilleach, VE 3,722** — *The stand of antlers grows at the gully's mouth* (Gleann nan Damh). Two autumns running, a good drive leaves the stacked antlers at the mouth of the glen tall enough for a boy to stand in their shadow at noon, the household's plain mark of what the year's meat has cost the herd.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0053"><em>The deer-drives of the eastern forest</em>, 10 an Gearran, VE 3,720</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5044"></a>**5 an Giblean, VE 3,725** — *Dubhghall's throw goes wide* (Gleann nan Damh). In his first year at the gully's throat Dubhghall's throw strikes a young stag in the shoulder rather than the throat, and it takes his uncle and two others to finish it; he practises the throw all winter against a bundle of brush.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0053"><em>The deer-drives of the eastern forest</em>, 10 an Gearran, VE 3,720</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5042"><em>Dubhghall drives the gully alone for the first time</em>, 4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,720</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5045"></a>**7 am Màrt, VE 3,740** — *Dubhghall takes the head of the drive* (Gleann nan Damh). When his uncle's knees will no longer hold him through a whole autumn morning, Dubhghall takes the head of the line at the gully, exacting in one thing only: that no young man stand carelessly.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5044"><em>Dubhghall's throw goes wide</em>, 5 an Giblean, VE 3,725</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5046"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,750** — *Dubhghall's uncle dies* (Gleann nan Damh). Worn thin by winters and no longer able to stand a whole autumn morning at the gully, Dubhghall's uncle dies and is buried within sight of the glen's mouth, close enough that his grandchildren can point to the rise from the stand of horn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0053"><em>The deer-drives of the eastern forest</em>, 10 an Gearran, VE 3,720</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5045"><em>Dubhghall takes the head of the drive</em>, 7 am Màrt, VE 3,740</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5047"></a>**4 an Cèitean, VE 3,757** — *Dubhghall's grandson's dog dies* (Cnoc fhionn). A dog that has slept across the boy's feet every night since it was weaned lies down by the hearth one evening and does not rise the next morning, found stiff and cold before the household is properly awake.
- <a id="ev-EI-5048"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,757** — *The boy digs the dog a grave and sets a shell at its head* (Cnoc fhionn). On the dry rise above the house, the boy digs a grave the length of a dog, lays it on its side as a sleeping dog lies, and sets at its head a sea-shell kept idle on a hearth-shelf for years, telling no one beforehand and asking no leave.
- <a id="ev-EI-5049"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,758** — *An old woman questions the dog's grave* (Cnoc fhionn). At a gathering of the near hearths an older woman asks the boy, not unkindly, whether he means to give every lost lamb a shell as well; he answers only that the dog slept at his feet for nine years and a lamb never did, and she allows it is answer enough.
- <a id="ev-EI-5050"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, VE 3,759** — *Dubhghall's grandson asks why no one hunts the geese* (Eilean ghorm). Watching the grey line come in over the water one still evening, the boy asks his grandfather why no household takes the geese of Eilean ghorm for meat; Dubhghall answers only that a people who stop leaving what they have always left are no longer quite the people they were.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5046"><em>Dubhghall's uncle dies</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,750</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5051"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, VE 3,760** — *Two more households bury dogs at Cnoc fhionn* (Cnoc fhionn). Within a few years of the first grave, two neighbouring households bury their own dogs the same way, a shell at the head and a proper grave dug, and the custom begins to travel hearth to hearth through the hill country.
- <a id="ev-EI-5052"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, VE 3,760** — *Dubhghall dies at Cnoc fhionn* (Cnoc fhionn). Dubhghall dies in his sixty-fifth year among his daughter's family, remembered at his own leaving for thirty autumns of driving the glen without losing a man to horn or wet ground; his grandson sets the last of his kept shells at the old man's head.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0053"><em>The deer-drives of the eastern forest</em>, 10 an Gearran, VE 3,720</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5050"><em>Dubhghall's grandson asks why no one hunts the geese</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, VE 3,759</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5053"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,760** — *A shell set at Dubhghall's head* (Cnoc fhionn). Dubhghall's grandson sets a shell at his grandfather's head at his burying, the last of a small store kept since the dog's grave, saying the old man deserved no less than a dog.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5052"><em>Dubhghall dies at Cnoc fhionn</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, VE 3,760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5054"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,770** — *The young man of the northern moor builds a boat for Eilean ghorm* (Eilean ghorm). In a season of want, a young man of the northern moor spends a hard winter building a hide boat in secret and puts out alone one grey morning for the geese's island, telling no one what the boat is for.
- <a id="ev-I-0054"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,771** — *The first dog graves* (Cnoc fhionn). At Cnoc fhionn in the east dogs are buried beside people, each with a shell at its head. No beast was given a grave on Dia-thìr before.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5047"><em>Dubhghall's grandson's dog dies</em>, 4 an Cèitean, VE 3,757</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5048"><em>The boy digs the dog a grave and sets a shell at its head</em>, 30 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,757</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5049"><em>An old woman questions the dog's grave</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,758</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5051"><em>Two more households bury dogs at Cnoc fhionn</em>, 5 an t-Sultain, VE 3,760</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EI-5052"><em>Dubhghall dies at Cnoc fhionn</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, VE 3,760</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EI-5053"><em>A shell set at Dubhghall's head</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5055"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, VE 3,771** — *The young man does not come back a hunter* (Eilean ghorm). The fate of the young man who sailed for Eilean ghorm is told three ways at three hearths and agreed by none of them; he is remembered not as one who found good hunting, but as a warning the country keeps without understanding it.
- <a id="ev-I-0055"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,821** — *The geese of Eilean ghorm* (Eilean ghorm). The grey geese that winter on Eilean ghorm come into the tellings for the first time. They come in with the first storm and leave with the last, and none hunts them there.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5050"><em>Dubhghall's grandson asks why no one hunts the geese</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, VE 3,759</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5054"><em>The young man of the northern moor builds a boat for Eilean ghorm</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,770</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5055"><em>The young man does not come back a hunter</em>, 14 an t-Sultain, VE 3,771</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5056"></a>**12 an Cèitean, VE 3,822** — *The geese read for the turn of the winter* (Eilean ghorm). Households that watch the grey geese of Eilean ghorm close enough learn to read the turn of the winter in their leaving, which comes a day or two ahead of the year's last storm.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0055"><em>The geese of Eilean ghorm</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 3,821</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5057"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,870** — *The mole at Skell stands nine hundred years* (Seann Skell). Mended and lengthened season on season since the old stone-judge first set it, the mole at Skell runs further out into the Abhainn naomh than any one lifetime could have carried it, and a woman of the landing walks its length each evening to look for any stone the current has worked loose.
- <a id="ev-EI-5058"></a>**15 am Màrt, VE 3,871** — *A woman walks the mole at Skell each evening* (Seann Skell). A woman of Skell who keeps the mole's stones walks its length each evening at the turn of the tide, looking for any stone the current has worked loose.
- <a id="ev-EI-5059"></a>**4 an Gearran, VE 3,872** — *Every mooring taken at Skell* (Seann Skell). At Skell on the Abhainn naomh, the greatest landing of the people of the shore, every mooring behind the mole is taken one autumn, hulls lying three and four deep along its sheltered face, and the smoke of the landing's hearths hangs over the river's mouth from dawn to dark.
- <a id="ev-I-0056"></a>**8 an Cèitean, VE 3,872** — *The widest reach of the Seann-Dhaoine* (Seann Skell). At their height the Seann-Dhaoine hold every coast of the island: the ten places whose names begin with Seann, and the islands off them. Their greatest landing is at Seann Skell, up the Abhainn naomh, where the mole already stands.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5057"><em>The mole at Skell stands nine hundred years</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,870</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EI-5058"><em>A woman walks the mole at Skell each evening</em>, 15 am Màrt, VE 3,871</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5059"><em>Every mooring taken at Skell</em>, 4 an Gearran, VE 3,872</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0057"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,922** — *The warm springs used* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). Stone basins are set into the springs at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh. The people buried near them have old breaks that knitted clean. Here the sick of Dia-thìr are first brought for healing.
- <a id="ev-EI-5501"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,924** — *A leg set under the warm water*. At Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh the keeper of the basins sets a leg broken through the skin under the warm water of the third basin, binds it tight with wet bark and cord, and turns the man twice a day for a season; he walks out on a stick before the winter turns.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0057"><em>The warm springs used</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,922</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5502"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,930** — *The keeper of the basins judges a wound by its smell* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The keeper of the warm basins tells by the colour of a wound, and its smell when the dressing comes off, whether it wants the second basin or the third or neither, and has no words for the telling.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0057"><em>The warm springs used</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,922</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5503"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, VE 3,949** — *The youth of the south-east asks to go down*. A youth not yet grown to his height asks to be the one let down into the eastern shaft at Toll-dubh, and two women of the south-east plait a rope for it from the hides of three oxen.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5504"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, VE 3,950** — *The lamp goes small in the eastern shaft*. The youth is let down into the eastern shaft on the plaited rope with a lamp of fat in a hollowed stone; the lamp goes small and the dark closes over it, the rope runs out to its last knot and hangs, and after a long while it jerks twice and is hauled up slowly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5505"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, VE 3,950** — *The youth comes up ash-faced and silent*. The youth comes over the lip with his lamp out and his face the colour of ash, and never says, then or in all the years he lives, what was at the bottom; after him no one goes down again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0036"><em>The shaft of Toll-dubh in the south-east</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, VE 2,730</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5506"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, VE 3,960** — *The young keeper takes up the turning*. The old keeper of the basins dies and is buried on the slope nearest the water; a young woman who came up as a girl with a father whose ribs were stove in takes up the setting and the turning the next morning, and sets three bones that day.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0057"><em>The warm springs used</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,922</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5507"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, VE 3,965** — *A child's broken skull mended by the first basin*. A child fallen from a kiln wall is carried two days to the springs by its mother with the bone above its ear broken; the young keeper lays it by the steam of the first basin, washes the break and binds it loosely, and on the fourth morning it wakes and asks for food.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0057"><em>The warm springs used</em>, 6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 3,922</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5508"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, VE 3,970** — *Heated stones laid in the third basin in a dry summer* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). In a dry summer when the water runs low from the three mouths, the keepers of the basins lay stones heated in a fire into the third basin to bring it back to the warmth the sick need.
- <a id="ev-I-0058"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, VE 3,973** — *The gate of the outpost walled up* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). The single gate of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire is blocked with rubble from within. Those who did it left by another way, or did not leave.
- <a id="ev-EI-5509"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, VE 3,973** — *The last stone set by lamplight*. One man, left alone at Làrach an Dùin-fhaire's gate at dusk after the others have gone to other work within the walls, fits the last stones into the gap by a lamp burning down, and presses the last one home with the flat of his hand. Where he went after is not told.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0058"><em>The gate of the outpost walled up</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, VE 3,973</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5510"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, VE 3,990** — *The rope of the shaft cut up for mooring lines* (Toll-dubh). After the youth comes up silent, the plaited rope is cut up for mooring lines, and the grown people of the south-east walk wider of the shaft's lip than before.
- <a id="ev-EI-5511"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, VE 4,000** — *The youth will not let a lamp burn low* (Toll-dubh). The youth who went down the eastern shaft, grown and married at a landing two days south, is known for nothing strange except that he rises in the night to trim or put out any lamp burning low.

## The Years VE 4,001 – 4,500

- <a id="ev-I-0059"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, VE 4,023** — *Làrach an Dùin-fhaire abandoned* (Làrach an Dùin-fhaire). The outpost is deserted. It lay in ruin before the first trusty chronicles, and it is older than any dwelling of the Dia-thìrich. Who built it none knows.
- <a id="ev-EI-5512"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, VE 4,030** — *The kerbed way greens over*. With no one going down off the spur, the grass creeps in over the slabs of the kerbed way from its edges, and the kerbs show through the turf like the bones of a thing half buried.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0059"><em>Làrach an Dùin-fhaire abandoned</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, VE 4,023</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5513"></a>**21 an Gearran, VE 4,074** — *A woman finds the cistern choked*. A woman of the three rings, going at first light to draw water for her sick father, finds the cistern full of whole cattle, unbutchered, their backs and bent legs breaking the dark water; no one of the rings can say who did it, and no one draws from it again.
- <a id="ev-I-0060"></a>**4 an Giblean, VE 4,074** — *The fortress cistern fouled* (Làrach an Dùin). The cistern of Làrach an Dùin is choked with the bones of cattle, thrown in whole. Its water had served four hundred people. No one draws from it again.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5513"><em>A woman finds the cistern choked</em>, 21 an Gearran, VE 4,074</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5514"></a>**12 am Màrt, VE 4,075** — *Water carried up the height every morning* (Làrach an Dùin). With the cistern of the three rings fouled, every household on the height carries its water up from the valley springs on its own back, a whole morning's labour every morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0060"><em>The fortress cistern fouled</em>, 4 an Giblean, VE 4,074</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5515"></a>**11 an Gearran, VE 4,100** — *The first households go down from the rings* (Làrach an Dùin). Some households of the three rings tire of the water-carrying before they tire of the height, and go down the track to the lower valleys, saying they go only for the winter.
- <a id="ev-EI-5516"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, VE 4,123** — *Fewer fires burn along Làrach an Dùin wall* (Làrach an Dùin). Through a hard winter the coast-people left within the three rings let the farthest fires along the middle wall go dark first, feeding what fuel is left toward those nearest the gate, so that the chain of lights along the rampart burns shorter and thicker each week that passes.
- <a id="ev-EI-5517"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, VE 4,124** — *The last fire in the rings is let go down* (Làrach an Dùin). The last of the coast-people still keeping Làrach an Dùin finds every other fire along the wall dark one morning, tends her own alone three days more, then spreads its embers thin across the stone and walks out through the gate and down toward the valleys, carrying nothing from the place she had not carried into it.
- <a id="ev-I-0061"></a>**6 am Màrt, VE 4,124** — *Làrach an Dùin abandoned* (Làrach an Dùin). The fortress is deserted in like manner, and is as much a riddle as the outpost. Whether both had the same builders has never been settled.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5515"><em>The first households go down from the rings</em>, 11 an Gearran, VE 4,100</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5516"><em>Fewer fires burn along Làrach an Dùin wall</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, VE 4,123</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5517"><em>The last fire in the rings is let go down</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, VE 4,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5518"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,126** — *Grass in the threshold of the rings* (Làrach an Dùin). Within a few winters of the last fire along the middle wall, grass finds a footing in the gate threshold of the three rings, where the feet of four hundred once kept the stone bare.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0061"><em>Làrach an Dùin abandoned</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 4,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5519"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,130** — *A grandfather of the western landing will not speak of the height* (Seann Skell). An old man long settled among shore kin who never went up answers his grandson's question about Làrach an Dùin only with the cold and the wind that found a man through doubled wool, and will say nothing of why he left it or whether he meant, at the time, to come back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0061"><em>Làrach an Dùin abandoned</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 4,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5520"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,135** — *A household from the rings comes down to Morn* (Seann Skell). A household of five comes down from the three rings to the kilns at Morn with nothing but what it can carry, its one ox lost on the scree; the landing takes it in, and the women are set to the kilns, where the younger learns in one morning that a kiln fire must smoke and not flame.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0061"><em>Làrach an Dùin abandoned</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 4,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5521"></a>**13 an Cèitean, VE 4,150** — *The southern middens grow faster than living memory* (Seann Chwen). As more of the coast-people settle at the shore than the shore has ever held, the middens of the southern landing thicken season on season with the ordinary leavings of a people's swelling numbers, and a landing once counted by the dozen comes to be counted by the score.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0061"><em>Làrach an Dùin abandoned</em>, 6 am Màrt, VE 4,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5522"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, VE 4,150** — *The son's wife learns a kiln must not flame* (Seann Mhorn). The keeper of the middle kiln at Morn leads a woman new down from the heights by the wrist to a smouldering kiln and holds her hand over its rack until she understands what three tellings in words had not taught her.
- <a id="ev-EI-5523"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,160** — *A girl from the heights sees the sea* (Seann Mhorn). A girl of eight born within the innermost ring is lifted onto a rock above Morn by her grandfather and turned to face the sea, and asks, after a long look, whether it ever stops moving.
- <a id="ev-EI-5524"></a>**16 am Màrt, VE 4,170** — *A worked stone kept on a shore shelf* (Eilean dhearg). An old man come down from a height keeps on a shelf at the shore a worked stone no one there has a use for, and it is laid in the stone box with him when his time comes.
- <a id="ev-EI-5525"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, VE 4,175** — *Three men climb to the temple with prising-bars* (Làrach an Teampaill). Three men of the last kin that still tends the temple climb its steps on a grey autumn morning with bars of seasoned oak shod with bone, the eldest of them a man past sixty who has climbed on the shortest morning every year of his life.
- <a id="ev-EI-5526"></a>**1 an Gearran, VE 4,175** — *The altar's top stone is prised free* (Làrach an Teampaill). Working the better part of the morning, two of the three break out the old clay from the sockets with the points of their bars while the eldest stands with his hands flat on the stone, and a while past noon they lift it whole from the sockets it has held since before anyone could remember.
- <a id="ev-I-0062"></a>**5 an Gearran, VE 4,175** — *The temple altar stripped* (Làrach an Teampaill). The top stone of the altar at Làrach an Teampaill is prised off and carried away; the sockets that held it are sharp still. It has never been found, and what was cut on it, if anything, is not known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5525"><em>Three men climb to the temple with prising-bars</em>, 19 am Faoilleach, VE 4,175</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5526"><em>The altar's top stone is prised free</em>, 1 an Gearran, VE 4,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5527"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, VE 4,175** — *The altar stone is carried west out of sight* (Làrach an Teampaill). Slung between the three in a net of hide rope on the same bars, the altar stone is carried down the platform steps and over the shoulder of the hill to the west; it is never found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062"><em>The temple altar stripped</em>, 5 an Gearran, VE 4,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5528"></a>**27 an Gearran, VE 4,180** — *The temple platform goes untended* (Làrach an Teampaill). No one of that kin climbs the temple steps on the shortest morning again; grass comes in between the platform's fitted stones, and the easy last step that every child of the valley once found with a bare foot in the dark is lost under turf.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062"><em>The temple altar stripped</em>, 5 an Gearran, VE 4,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5529"></a>**28 am Màrt, VE 4,190** — *A cairn built below the empty sockets* (Làrach an Teampaill). The eldest of the three who prised the altar goes up alone years after and spends most of a day building a small cairn of loose stone below the empty sockets, capped square, and comes down with his hands scraped raw, and does not say what it is for.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0062"><em>The temple altar stripped</em>, 5 an Gearran, VE 4,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5530"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,190** — *The easy last step lost under turf* (Làrach an Teampaill). The last step of the temple platform, flush with the moor, which every child of the valley once found with a bare foot in the dark, is lost under turf, and the climb begins now with a stumble.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062"><em>The temple altar stripped</em>, 5 an Gearran, VE 4,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5531"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,196** — *Eòghann born to the keeper's hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann is born the second child of the household that keeps the bag and Poit an Teine at Tobar dhìreach, not first looked to for the keeping while his elder sister lives.
- <a id="ev-EI-5532"></a>**27 an Gearran, VE 4,210** — *Eòghann counts the coals into his palm as a child* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann, free of the keeping as a younger son, counts the three coals into his own small palm long before anyone asks it of him, turning them over for the plain pleasure of a smooth thing in the hand.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5531"><em>Eòghann born to the keeper's hearth</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,196</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5533"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, VE 4,216** — *The keeping falls to Eòghann* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann's sister dies of a fever in her nineteenth year, and the bag of three dark coals and the recital pass to Eòghann on his father's death soon after; he is twenty.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5532"><em>Eòghann counts the coals into his palm as a child</em>, 27 an Gearran, VE 4,210</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5534"></a>**26 an Giblean, VE 4,216** — *Eòghann's sister dies and his father is buried* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann's elder sister dies of a fever in her nineteenth year, and his father is buried beside Leac na Fèithe the same season, so that the keeping comes to Eòghann at twenty.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5533"><em>The keeping falls to Eòghann</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, VE 4,216</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5535"></a>**28 am Màrt, VE 4,220** — *Eòghann marries Dearbhail* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann takes Dearbhail of the lake-shore line, who keeps his fire-pot and his hearth through the long absences his walking keeps him to.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5534"><em>Eòghann's sister dies and his father is buried</em>, 26 an Giblean, VE 4,216</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5536"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,221** — *Gual airgid carried to the home river and two more* (Tobar dhìreach). In his first years of keeping Eòghann carries gual airgid to the Abhainn ghorm below Tobar dhìreach, to two rivers besides, and to a mountain tarn, in case the water nearest the hearth had never been fairly asked; none answers him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5535"><em>Eòghann marries Dearbhail</em>, 28 am Màrt, VE 4,220</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5537"></a>**25 an Cèitean, VE 4,224** — *A mountain tarn tried for the silver*. Among the waters Eòghann tries gual airgid against is a mountain tarn that is no river at all but holds, by the telling, water enough to be worth the asking; it does not answer.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5536"><em>Gual airgid carried to the home river and two more</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,221</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5538"></a>**2 an Giblean, VE 4,225** — *Eòghann keeps the old custom of the shore* (Tobar dhìreach). With nothing newly occurring to him, Eòghann carries the three dark coals north to the shore his father once brought him to, to throw them into the sea in the old way, out of a custom kept past most keepers' belief in it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5537"><em>A mountain tarn tried for the silver</em>, 25 an Cèitean, VE 4,224</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5539"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,225** — *The three coals thrown into the sea again for nothing*. Eòghann throws the silver, the untried, and gual bogha-froise into the grey swell off the northern shore in the falling light, and wades in after them to find them as dark and salt-wet as they went in.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5538"><em>Eòghann keeps the old custom of the shore</em>, 2 an Giblean, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5540"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, VE 4,225** — *Eòghann walks home through two days of rain*. Eòghann turns south for Tobar dhìreach the morning after the casting, walking two wet days over moor and birch scrub with his mind on nothing beyond the ground in front of him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5539"><em>The three coals thrown into the sea again for nothing</em>, 4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0062a"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225** — *The silver coal in the river* (Abhainn ghorm). Eòghann of the Mason's line drinks from the Abhainn ghorm below Tobar dhìreach and says, 'This water tastes different from the sea water.' He throws the three unlit coals into the stream, and the coal with the sheen of silver takes fire in the current and burns silver under the water. The coal of fire and the rainbow coal lie dark.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5538"><em>Eòghann keeps the old custom of the shore</em>, 2 an Giblean, VE 4,225</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5539"><em>The three coals thrown into the sea again for nothing</em>, 4 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,225</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5540"><em>Eòghann walks home through two days of rain</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5541"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225** — *Eòghann kneels and drinks at the crossing* (Tobar dhìreach). Thirsty and tired on the last stretch of the road home, Eòghann kneels at the crossing of the Abhainn ghorm below Tobar dhìreach and drinks, and says aloud, to no one, that this water tastes different from the sea water.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5540"><em>Eòghann walks home through two days of rain</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5542"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225** — *Gual airgid catches under the current* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann throws the three dark coals into the river at the crossing without weighing the throw, and gual airgid catches beneath the surface, a pale fire standing in the current that the water cannot quench.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5541"><em>Eòghann kneels and drinks at the crossing</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5543"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225** — *The two dark coals found on a gravel bar* (Tobar dhìreach). Gual teine and the rainbow, rolled on past Eòghann by the current in the dark, are found at first light lodged cold against a bar of gravel a stone's throw below the crossing, and carried home in the bag as dark as they went into the water.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5542"><em>Gual airgid catches under the current</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5544"></a>**27 an Gearran, VE 4,226** — *The fifth coal named at the recital* (Tobar dhìreach). At the next telling of the Line, Eòghann speaks the new line into the recital: the sea, the height, the earth and a man's own blood have answered, and now the river has taken the fifth, given rather than thrown to it, and the valley names it gual airgid.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5543"><em>The two dark coals found on a gravel bar</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5545"></a>**28 am Màrt, VE 4,226** — *The silver burns on under the crossing* (Abhainn ghorm). Gual airgid goes on burning under the current at the shallow crossing below Tobar dhìreach, a low pale light any traveller may kneel at the bank and see on a dark evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5546"></a>**26 an Giblean, VE 4,230** — *Travellers come to see the fire under the water* (Tobar dhìreach). Word of the pale fire standing under the current draws travellers to the crossing below Tobar dhìreach in numbers greater than the ford had ever seen, some kneeling to drink the same water Eòghann drank without finding it tastes to them any different.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5547"></a>**25 an Cèitean, VE 4,240** — *Eòghann tells the taste cannot be looked for* (Tobar dhìreach). Pressed to say what he tasted in the river, Eòghann owns that he cannot put it into words and holds that a man cannot go looking for that taste and find it sooner than he himself found it, kneeling thirsty.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5544"><em>The fifth coal named at the recital</em>, 27 an Gearran, VE 4,226</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5548"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, VE 4,245** — *Eòghann tries gual teine against flint* (Tobar dhìreach).
