In his later keeping Eòghann strikes gual teine against flint more than once, hoping the snap of a hand the tellers spoke of might be struck rather than fallen into, and gets from it no more than the ordinary spark any stone gives a blade.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5547"><em>Eòghann tells the taste cannot be looked for</em>, 25 an Cèitean, VE 4,240</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5549"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,262** — *Eòghann dies at his own hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Eòghann dies in his six-and-sixtieth year at Tobar dhìreach, Poit an Teine burning near him, his last words not of the coals but of the crossing, asking whether the water still ran clear and the light still stood under it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0062a"><em>The silver coal in the river</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,225</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5548"><em>Eòghann tries gual teine against flint</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, VE 4,245</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5550"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,262** — *The bag passes on with two coals still dark* (Tobar dhìreach). The leather bag, with gual teine and gual bogha-froise still unanswered, passes from Eòghann's grave to a younger kinsman of the line, as it passed from Cormac's before him.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5549"><em>Eòghann dies at his own hearth</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,262</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5551"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, VE 4,270** — *Fewer of the coast-people climb to the temple* (Làrach an Teampaill). In the years before the temple stands empty for good, those of the landings who still climb to Làrach an Teampaill go up fewer at a time and stay a shorter while at the top, as a household goes on setting a place at table for a while after the one who sat in it has stopped coming.
- <a id="ev-I-0063"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,275** — *Làrach an Teampaill abandoned* (Làrach an Teampaill). The temple is deserted. It is older than any faith that has a name, and its altar looks to the central mountains and the vein beneath them, away from the sea.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5551"><em>Fewer of the coast-people climb to the temple</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, VE 4,270</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5552"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, VE 4,276** — *A woman climbs to the temple with empty hands* (Làrach an Teampaill). A woman of the landings climbs the temple's steps alone at first light and comes down again at evening with nothing in her hands either time, and no one after her is known to climb to Làrach an Teampaill again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0063"><em>Làrach an Teampaill abandoned</em>, 7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,275</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5553"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, VE 4,290** — *Grass takes the temple platform* (Làrach an Teampaill). With no foot left to keep it short, the grass between the temple platform's fitted stones grows up thick, and the altar's empty sockets are left to fill and empty again with nothing but whatever season sends into them.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0063"><em>Làrach an Teampaill abandoned</em>, 7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,275</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5554"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,300** — *Whole kin-groups come down from the abandoned heights* (Seann Chwen). Where ones and single families once drifted down from the empty heights to settle at the shore, whole kin-groups now come down together, until the landing at Cwen holds more people at once than any landing has held before.
- <a id="ev-EI-5555"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, VE 4,300** — *A rower teaches the gulls' warning* (Seann Dunn). Rowers of Slighe-mhara àrsaidh keep a plain word for anyone new to the stretch north of the cape: watch the gulls before you watch the sky, for the birds leave that water before a man in it feels what is coming.
- <a id="ev-EI-5556"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,320** — *No new work raised out of sight of salt water* (Seann Chwen). After the high places are left, the people of the landings raise no new work anywhere out of sight of salt water, and the shore takes back all the labour the heights had drawn away.
- <a id="ev-I-0064"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,325** — *The Seann-Dhaoine keep to the shore* (Seann Chwen). The high places are left, and every new work of the Seann-Dhaoine is made within sight of salt water. The middens at the southern Seann Chwen begin to grow as fast as those of Seann Dunn once did.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5554"><em>Whole kin-groups come down from the abandoned heights</em>, 22 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,300</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-5556"><em>No new work raised out of sight of salt water</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,320</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5557"></a>**25 an Cèitean, VE 4,340** — *The midden at Cwen outgrows the midden at Dunn* (Seann Chwen). The midden below the southern landing at Cwen, thickened season on season by the swelling numbers settled there, grows past the midden at Dunn, which had for a lifetime and more been the largest heap of shell and bone the coast could show.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0064"><em>The Seann-Dhaoine keep to the shore</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,325</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5558"></a>**26 an Giblean, VE 4,350** — *A landing once counted by the dozen is counted by the score* (Seann Chwen). Two rowers of the sea-way, meeting off a landing-stone, trade the season's news: more households at Cwen than either can remember from a single year before, and a landing further north near empty of the families that once worked it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0064"><em>The Seann-Dhaoine keep to the shore</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,325</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0064a"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,375** — *The ancient sea-way* (Seann Dunn). The boats of the Seann-Dhaoine keep a lane along the south-east coast, from the river mouth below Seann Dunn round the cape where Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg now stands to the bay of Ceann chaol. Flat landing-stones lie along it a day's rowing apart, some grooved still by hauled keels. The Dia-thìrich call it Slighe-mhara àrsaidh, the ancient sea-way, and the fishers of that coast keep to it yet.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EI-5555"><em>A rower teaches the gulls' warning</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, VE 4,300</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5559"></a>**28 am Màrt, VE 4,380** — *The sea-way's landing-stones grooved by keels* (Seann Dunn). Season on season of hauled keels wear clear grooves into the flat landing-stones of Slighe-mhara àrsaidh along the south-east coast, so that a rower of that lane comes to know each stone by its wear as surely as by its place along the shore.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0064a"><em>The ancient sea-way</em>, 7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,375</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5560"></a>**15 an Cèitean, VE 4,390** — *A father teaches his son the sea-way stone by stone* (Seann Dunn). A rower of Slighe-mhara àrsaidh carries his son in the bow through a whole season's rowing, naming each landing-stone as it comes until the boy's own eye can find the next one before his father's voice does, the same teaching the lane is given, before and after, to every rower's son.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0064a"><em>The ancient sea-way</em>, 7 am Faoilleach, VE 4,375</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5561"></a>**13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,400** — *Rathnait born to the valleys about the crack* (Àth gharbh). Rathnait is born the third child of a household two ridges east of Tobar dhìreach, of no line that keeps a fire-pot or counts fathers back to the mason by name, but of the valleys about the crack all the same.
- <a id="ev-EI-5562"></a>**18 am Màrt, VE 4,410** — *The valleys' dead laid facing the mountains* (Àth gharbh). The households of the high valleys lay their dead in the ground on their side with the knees drawn up and the face toward the central mountains, with an uncut stone set on end at the head and no mark on it.
- <a id="ev-I-0065"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425** — *The hill-folk of the vein* (Àth gharbh). In the high valleys about the crack dwells a people other than the Seann-Dhaoine, who call themselves Clann nan Dè, the godkin. They bury their dead in the ground and not on islands, and they cut no script. Whether they shared the island with the Seann-Dhaoine or came after them, no telling knows; their own word, later, is that they were always there.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5561"><em>Rathnait born to the valleys about the crack</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,400</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-5562"><em>The valleys' dead laid facing the mountains</em>, 18 am Màrt, VE 4,410</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5563"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,425** — *An elder doubts the new name will last* (Àth gharbh). At Oidhche an Dealanaich an old woman of the ford hears the households called Clann nan Dè for the first time and will not say the word herself, having watched other names tried at other gatherings in her own long life and none of them outlast the fire that first warmed them into being said.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0065"><em>The hill-folk of the vein</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5561"><em>Rathnait born to the valleys about the crack</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5564"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,425** — *An old man of the west gives the name Clann nan Dè* (Àth gharbh). At the gathering on Oidhche an Dealanaich an old man of the western household answers a stranger's question with a word for the whole of the gathered valleys: Clann nan Dè.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0065"><em>The hill-folk of the vein</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5563"><em>An elder doubts the new name will last</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,425</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5565"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, VE 4,440** — *The name carried to hearths not at the gathering*. The name Clann nan Dè is said the next night of the lightning at hearths that were not at the western gathering, carried to them as a coal is carried from one hearth to a cold one three valleys off.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0065"><em>The hill-folk of the vein</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5564"><em>An old man of the west gives the name Clann nan Dè</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,425</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5566"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,450** — *Clann nan Dè settles into ordinary use* (Àth gharbh). By the time Rathnait is old enough to sit among the elders at her own hearth's turn to hold the gathering, the name Clann nan Dè is said across the valleys about the crack as plainly and as unremarked as any older name tied to a single ridge or ford.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0065"><em>The hill-folk of the vein</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5565"><em>The name carried to hearths not at the gathering</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, VE 4,440</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-5567"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, VE 4,468** — *Rathnait dies among the valleys she named* (Àth gharbh). Rathnait dies at her own household's hearth, having carried the word she first heard tried at a stranger's fire into ordinary use across the whole of the valleys about the crack.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0065"><em>The hill-folk of the vein</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, VE 4,425</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-5566"><em>Clann nan Dè settles into ordinary use</em>, 12 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,450</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0066"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475** — *The first small burning* (Àth gharbh). At Àth gharbh a sliver of the coloured coal is burnt to a bead in a peat fire by a household not of the Mason's line. It burns black-flamed like any other coal, and the hearthstone round it is stained through with colour. No older burning of the coal by other hands is known. It is a small thing: one sliver, one fire.
- <a id="ev-EI-6001"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, VE 4,475** — *Barabal burns the first sliver outside the line* (Àth gharbh). At Àth gharbh a woman named Barabal, keeping a bright stone given her as a child at a ford, sets it on her peat fire from idle curiosity; it burns black-flamed like any coal, and the hearthstone beneath it takes a stain of colour clean through its thickness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0066"><em>The first small burning</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6002"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,476** — *Barabal's husband's mother knows the stained stone* (Àth gharbh). Barabal's husband's mother turns the stained hearthstone over in the daylight at the door and says she once heard that Clann a' Chlachair kept coloured stones just such as this.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0066"><em>The first small burning</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6001"><em>Barabal burns the first sliver outside the line</em>, 21 an t-Samhain, VE 4,475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6003"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,482** — *Word of the stained hearthstone reaches Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). A fire-bearer carries the tale of Barabal's stained hearthstone to Clann a' Chlachair at Tobar dhìreach, and the woman who then keeps the bag hears it out and says only that a piece small enough to fit a boy's palm was small enough to lose.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0066"><em>The first small burning</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6002"><em>Barabal's husband's mother knows the stained stone</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,476</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6004"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, VE 4,490** — *Giorsal born at Achadh dhìreach* (Achadh dhìreach). Giorsal is born at Achadh dhìreach, ten miles west of the crack, to a household that keeps no fire-pot and counts no fathers back to the mason, and grows up on Aithris a' Chruthachaidh as every child of the valleys does.
- <a id="ev-EI-6005"></a>**18 an Gearran, VE 4,500** — *The stained hearthstone shown to travellers* (Àth gharbh). The stained hearthstone at Àth gharbh is shown to travellers who ask after it and to children who do not, a plain curiosity, until a later hand splits it to see whether the colour runs all the way through.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0066"><em>The first small burning</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475</a>.</span>

## The Years VE 4,501 – 5,000

- <a id="ev-EI-6006"></a>**19 am Màrt, VE 4,512** — *Barabal dies at Àth gharbh* (Àth gharbh). Barabal dies in her two-and-seventieth year at her own hearth, remembered by her own valley less as the woman who first burned an gual dathach than simply as an old grandmother among her kin.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0066"><em>The first small burning</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, VE 4,475</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6003"><em>Word of the stained hearthstone reaches Tobar dhìreach</em>, 11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,482</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6007"></a>**17 an Giblean, VE 4,520** — *Giorsal's grandmother shows her the bright stone* (Achadh dhìreach). Giorsal's grandmother shows her as a girl the scrap of coloured stone kept in a box at Achadh dhìreach three generations, calling it only the bright stone and saying nothing of what it is.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6004"><em>Giorsal born at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 4,490</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0067"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,525** — *The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach* (Achadh dhìreach). At Achadh dhìreach the hill-folk rub broken coal from the vein into the wool of the dead, and it takes streaks of a colour no plant dye makes. It is seldom done: one grave in some thirty.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6004"><em>Giorsal born at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 4,490</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6007"><em>Giorsal's grandmother shows her the bright stone</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6008"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,525** — *Giorsal begins rubbing coal into the wool of the dead* (Achadh dhìreach). Giorsal, who sees to the burials of her household, takes up the private habit of rubbing a little broken coloured coal into the wrapping wool of some of her dead, choosing perhaps one grave in thirty across her working years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0067"><em>The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,525</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6007"><em>Giorsal's grandmother shows her the bright stone</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6009"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, VE 4,540** — *Word of the stained wool reaches the line* (Tobar dhìreach). A trader carries the tale of Giorsal's stained burial-wool to Tobar dhìreach some fifteen years after it begins, and Clann a' Chlachair takes it as further proof that its own coloured coal is no longer the only piece the valleys hold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0067"><em>The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,525</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6008"><em>Giorsal begins rubbing coal into the wool of the dead</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,525</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6010"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,560** — *Giorsal dies and is given the office in her turn* (Achadh dhìreach). Giorsal dies in her seventieth year of a wasting sickness, and her own daughter, taught the office before her, rubs a sliver of the coloured stone into her mother's own wrapping as she had seen it done for others.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0067"><em>The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,525</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6009"><em>Word of the stained wool reaches the line</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, VE 4,540</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6011"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,560** — *A bright stone is found on the midden at Bral* (Seann Bhral). A woman of Bral, sifting the midden below her household's huts, turns up a small hard thing bright with more than one colour, unlike any shell or stone the heap has yielded before; no one of that household can say how long it lay there or how it came.
- <a id="ev-EI-6012"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, VE 4,561** — *Giorsal buried with a sliver rubbed into her wrapping* (Achadh dhìreach). Giorsal's daughter rubs a sliver of the bright stone into her mother's own wrapping at her burial, the office passing once from the hand that always gave it to the hand that had only received it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0067"><em>The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,525</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6010"><em>Giorsal dies and is given the office in her turn</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,560</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6013"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,565** — *The stone at Bral is kept among the household's trinkets* (Seann Bhral). The bright stone found on the midden at Bral is never set to any fire; it is kept awhile among the household's small keepings, admired and set aside, and passes out of particular notice as such finds do.
- <a id="ev-I-0068"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, VE 4,575** — *A sliver in a Seann Bhral midden* (Seann Bhral). A chip of the coloured coal, still staining the shell about it, is thrown on a midden at Seann Bhral on the far western coast. By gift, by trade or by theft a piece of the vein came to the Seann-Dhaoine; which, is not known.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6011"><em>A bright stone is found on the midden at Bral</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,560</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EI-6013"><em>The stone at Bral is kept among the household's trinkets</em>, 11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,565</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0068a"></a>**18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625** — *The Children of the Question* (Tobar dhìreach). The households of the high valleys begin to call the Mason's line Luchd-ceasnachaidh a' Ghuail Dhìomhair, the Inquisitors of the Mystic Coal, for their long questioning of the two dark coals; the lists shorten it to Clann na Ceiste, the Children of the Question. The kindred take the name, and Clann a' Chlachair is heard less after.
- <a id="ev-EI-6014"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, VE 4,625** — *Oscar names the line in jest* (Àth gharbh). At the gathering on Oidhche an Dealanaich, Oscar of Àth gharbh calls Clann a' Chlachair Luchd-ceasnachaidh a' Ghuail Dhìomhair, the long questioners of the secret coal, meaning it half as a joke against their long, fruitless asking of the two dark coals.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6015"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, VE 4,625** — *Colla takes the name* (Tobar dhìreach). Colla, keeper of the bag at Tobar dhìreach and five and thirty that year, takes up Oscar's long name for his line without the laughter that first carried it, and gives travellers the short form, Clann na Ceiste, the children of the question.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6014"><em>Oscar names the line in jest</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, VE 4,625</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6016"></a>**16 an Cèitean, VE 4,626** — *Colla gives the long name to a traveller* (Tobar dhìreach). Asked by a traveller what his people call themselves, Colla gives back Oscar's long name without the laughter, and says the short form Clann na Ceiste will serve.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6015"><em>Colla takes the name</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, VE 4,625</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6017"></a>**17 an Giblean, VE 4,640** — *Clann na Ceiste settles into ordinary use* (Tobar dhìreach). The households of the valleys take up calling Clann a' Chlachair simply Clann na Ceiste in their everyday talk, the older name Clann a' Chlachair heard less with each passing year.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6018"></a>**19 am Màrt, VE 4,655** — *Colla dies and hands on the bag* (Tobar dhìreach). Colla dies in his five-and-sixtieth year, having kept the bag some thirty years, and hands the keeping before the end to a son whose name the reciters, as with every father along that stretch of the line, keep from strangers.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6016"><em>Colla gives the long name to a traveller</em>, 16 an Cèitean, VE 4,626</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6019"></a>**18 an Gearran, VE 4,656** — *The mason's children heard for the last time as the line's own name* (Tobar dhìreach). At the recital held the winter after Colla's death, the reciters say both the old name and the new, Clann a' Chlachair and Clann na Ceiste together, before letting the newer name stand alone in every recital after.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0068a"><em>The Children of the Question</em>, 18 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,625</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0069"></a>**17 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,672** — *Carragh Cnoc bheag raised* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). A standing stone is raised, on which four words are afterwards found carved: Bha teine sa chloich, "there was fire in the stone."
- <a id="ev-EI-6020"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, VE 4,672** — *Lughaidh finds a new-cut stone in the western grass* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Driving his flock further west than his own hearth has grazed before, the shepherd Lughaidh comes on a standing stone raised so lately that the turned earth at its foot has not yet greened over, with no camp, path or tool-litter left by whatever hand set it there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0069"><em>Carragh Cnoc bheag raised</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6021"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, VE 4,672** — *Two hands on one stone* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Lughaidh reads a line of unfamiliar script on the stone's upper face, cut broad and level by one hand, and below it four words of his own tongue, Bha teine sa chloich, cut narrower and shallower by another; neither hand has left any other mark on the hillside.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6020"><em>Lughaidh finds a new-cut stone in the western grass</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, VE 4,672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6022"></a>**16 an Lùnastal, VE 4,673** — *Lughaidh's find carried hearth to hearth*. The tale of the new stone in the western grass passes from Lughaidh's own hearth to the next and on beyond it, the four words kept exact in every mouth that takes them up while the stone's own size and the manner of its finding grow with the telling.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6021"><em>Two hands on one stone</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, VE 4,672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6023"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, VE 4,674** — *Lughaidh's father asks what he moved*. Told of the new stone in the western grass, Lughaidh's father asks first whether the boy left anything of his own behind or moved any stone, and Lughaidh, stung, says he moved nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0069"><em>Carragh Cnoc bheag raised</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,672</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6022"><em>Lughaidh's find carried hearth to hearth</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, VE 4,673</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6024"></a>**6 an Gearran, VE 4,675** — *The words of the low cutting known at every hearth* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). By the winter after the western stone is found, every hearth that tells of it tells also what its four low words say, though no one of the valleys reads a sign and no one can say whose mouth first gave the words.
- <a id="ev-EI-6025"></a>**7 am Màrt, VE 4,676** — *A woman of the line sits three days before the western stone* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). A woman of Clann na Ceiste sits three days before the western stone to learn which of its two hands came first, and comes home saying both kept their counsel and she will not guess.
- <a id="ev-EI-6026"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,680** — *Clann na Ceiste claims the fire, and leaves the older line unread* (Tobar dhìreach). Word of the stone's four words reaches Tobar dhìreach, and the line holds the fire they name for its own, Teine a' Chlachair, while the broader script above them goes on unread, no eye at the line or beyond it able to say what hand cut it or when.
- <a id="ev-EI-6027"></a>**8 am Faoilleach, VE 4,700** — *A second stone found in the stony hills* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). A traveller crossing poor, broken ground further into the hills all but walks into a shorter stone before he sees it, and carries down word of three more words cut low upon it, Cuimhnich an teine, in what looks the same sure hand as the first stone's saying.
- <a id="ev-EI-6028"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,705** — *The line answers for a bidding cut to no one* (Tobar dhìreach). Asked by travellers whether the second stone's plain command speaks to them any clearer than the first, Clann na Ceiste answers each time the same: that the fire is theirs to remember whether the stone bade them or not, there being no other hand on the island that has minded it so long.
- <a id="ev-I-0070"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,718** — *The older face of Carragh Cnoc bheag* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). On the upper face of the stone runs a line of the unread script. The four Dia-thìris words lie lower, cut with a narrower tool by another hand. When that second hand came is not known.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6021"><em>Two hands on one stone</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, VE 4,672</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EI-6022"><em>Lughaidh's find carried hearth to hearth</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, VE 4,673</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EI-6024"><em>The words of the low cutting known at every hearth</em>, 6 an Gearran, VE 4,675</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6025"><em>A woman of the line sits three days before the western stone</em>, 7 am Màrt, VE 4,676</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6026"><em>Clann na Ceiste claims the fire, and leaves the older line unread</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6029"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,720** — *Lughaidh dies at his own hearth*. Lughaidh dies in his own seventieth year, remembered by his own valley chiefly as the shepherd who first said the stone's four words aloud on the hillside where they stand.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0069"><em>Carragh Cnoc bheag raised</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,672</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6023"><em>Lughaidh's father asks what he moved</em>, 14 an t-Sultain, VE 4,674</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6030"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,720** — *The four words said standing at the gathering* (Tobar dhìreach). At that year's gathering a young man of the line says Bha teine sa chloich aloud, standing, before the whole crowd for what the tellers hold to be the first time, the saying having come to him by the same slow road as every other hearth, from mouth to mouth, back to a shepherd fifty years gone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0070"><em>The older face of Carragh Cnoc bheag</em>, 11 an Lùnastal, VE 4,718</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0071"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, VE 4,770** — *Colbh Cnoc chiar raised* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). A second stone is raised, bearing only three words: Cuimhnich an teine, "remember the fire." Who is bidden, and why, none has ever said.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6027"><em>A second stone found in the stony hills</em>, 8 am Faoilleach, VE 4,700</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EI-6028"><em>The line answers for a bidding cut to no one</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,705</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6031"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, VE 4,770** — *The three words of the second stone taken as meant for the line* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). The line at Tobar dhìreach answers every traveller who asks that the fire is theirs to remember whether the second stone bids them or not, and that they are glad enough to take the bidding as meant for them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0071"><em>Colbh Cnoc chiar raised</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, VE 4,770</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6032"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, VE 4,785** — *Mòrnait born at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). Mòrnait is born into a household gathered about Clann na Ceiste's own hearth without ever holding its coals, and grows up on Aithris a' Chruthachaidh and the two new sayings both, already part of the ordinary stock of what every child of the valleys knows by then.
- <a id="ev-EI-6033"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,805** — *Mòrnait carries fire to the second stone* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Mòrnait makes the hard day's walk into the stony hills with a coal from the line's own pot wrapped close against the wet, and builds at the foot of Colbh Cnoc chiar a ring of fire-cracked stones in which she lights and keeps a hearth-sized fire.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6032"><em>Mòrnait born at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 4,785</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0072"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812** — *A ring of fire-stones round the pillar* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). The ground about Colbh Cnoc chiar is trodden hard in a ring and paved with fire-cracked stones. Fires the size of hearths are kept there again and again. Nothing else is left.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6032"><em>Mòrnait born at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, VE 4,785</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6033"><em>Mòrnait carries fire to the second stone</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,805</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6034"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,812** — *The ring at the pillar is kept and grows a path* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Mòrnait returns to the ring at Colbh Cnoc chiar year on year, joined in time by others who come to sit an evening by the fire before going their own ways, until a worn path runs to it across the broken ground and the ash within the stones lies black and deep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0072"><em>A ring of fire-stones round the pillar</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6033"><em>Mòrnait carries fire to the second stone</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,805</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6035"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, VE 4,820** — *Mòrnait holds the fire is kept, not questioned* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). Asked more than once whether her fire is some new trial of the old riddle, Mòrnait answers that the stone asked only to be remembered, not questioned, there being questioning enough already given the two dark coals by better keepers than herself.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0072"><em>A ring of fire-stones round the pillar</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6034"><em>The ring at the pillar is kept and grows a path</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,812</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6036"></a>**9 an Giblean, VE 4,830** — *Others come to sit by Mòrnait's fire* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). As word of the fire at the second stone goes about the valleys, others walk the hard day into the stony hills to sit a night or a day by Mòrnait's fire before going home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0072"><em>A ring of fire-stones round the pillar</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6035"><em>Mòrnait holds the fire is kept, not questioned</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, VE 4,820</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6037"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, VE 4,850** — *Mòrnait's last walk to the ring* (Colbh Cnoc chiar). In her sixty-fifth year Mòrnait makes the walk to Colbh Cnoc chiar for the last time, and tells the few who sit with her that evening she does not know what the stone remembers, only that she has kept it as well as she knew how.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0072"><em>A ring of fire-stones round the pillar</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6036"><em>Others come to sit by Mòrnait's fire</em>, 9 an Giblean, VE 4,830</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6038"></a>**11 am Màrt, VE 4,850** — *Mòrnait dies, and her daughter takes up the keeping* (Tobar dhìreach). Mòrnait dies at her own hearth some weeks after her last walk, and her daughter, and after her the daughter's own children, take up the walk to the ring in her stead, less often than Mòrnait kept it but often enough that the fire does not go cold.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0072"><em>A ring of fire-stones round the pillar</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, VE 4,812</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6037"><em>Mòrnait's last walk to the ring</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, VE 4,850</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0073"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851** — *Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised* (Calbh Cnoc ghorm). A third stone is raised, and on it the whole of the saying: Cha do thàinig sinn; bha sinn ann. Here, it may be, the belief was first spoken.
- <a id="ev-EI-6039"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,851** — *Ciannait finds the third stone standing* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Ciannait, driving her household's beasts down to the autumn stubble, finds a squared pillar newly standing on the rise by the drove-road where no stone had stood the year before, and reads aloud, alone but for a boy of her own kin, the four words cut low on its face and the whole saying beneath them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6040"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,852** — *Ciannait's brother's boy asks if the stone will stand* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Ciannait's brother's boy asks whether the new-found pillar will still be standing come morning; she tells him a stone is not a fire and has never yet been known to go out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6039"><em>Ciannait finds the third stone standing</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6041"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, VE 4,853** — *The rise takes the name Achadh a' Chalbh* (Achadh a' Chalbh). The hearths that gather to look at the new pillar begin to call the rise Achadh a' Chalbh, a name that settles into use before any household troubles to remember which mouth first gave it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6042"></a>**21 an Gearran, VE 4,854** — *The whole saying said standing for the first time* (Achadh a' Chalbh). At a gathering of some thirty households kept at Achadh a' Chalbh on Oidhche an Dealanaich, an old woman of a neighbouring valley says the sayings of all three stones together before a crowd, and ties the third saying to Aithris a' Chruthachaidh's grass-people and the island as their only root.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6040"><em>Ciannait's brother's boy asks if the stone will stand</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, VE 4,852</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6043"></a>**22 am Màrt, VE 4,854** — *An old woman says the three sayings as one* (Achadh a' Chalbh). At the first gathering kept at the pillar an old woman of a hearth two valleys east says the sayings of the three stones together for the first time, and says after them that the stone says in fewer words what Aithris a' Chruthachaidh always said.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6044"></a>**20 an Giblean, VE 4,857** — *The gathering at the column kept a second year, and a third* (Achadh a' Chalbh). More households come to keep the dark of the year at Achadh a' Chalbh than came the winter before, and the ground about the pillar's foot begins to wear bare under their standing, so that within Ciannait's own lifetime the column becomes the one gathering-ground of that whole stretch of country.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6042"><em>The whole saying said standing for the first time</em>, 21 an Gearran, VE 4,854</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6045"></a>**19 an Cèitean, VE 4,862** — *Seathan born to the keeper's hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan is born at Tobar dhìreach, the only son of the keeper of gual teine and the rainbow, and has gual teine in his hands from earliest childhood as every child of that hearth has had it before him.
- <a id="ev-EI-6046"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,865** — *A market grows up at the column's gatherings* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Traders begin setting hides, salt and wool out on cloths spread over the trampled ground at Achadh a' Chalbh on the two days a year the crowds are greatest, taking their goods up again each evening, for no one yet thinks to leave anything standing there overnight but the stone.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6047"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,868** — *A boy of the keeper's hearth hears of the third stone* (Tobar dhìreach). At Tobar dhìreach a fire-bearer carries the first word of the pillar and its saying to the keeper's own hearth, and a boy not yet six turns gual teine in his fingers as he listens, asking his mother whether the coal and the stone's saying come from the one place.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6045"><em>Seathan born to the keeper's hearth</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 4,862</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6048"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, VE 4,870** — *The saying carried to the northern shore* (Achadh a' Chalbh). A woman of the northern shore, come south to trade hides for salt at one of Achadh a' Chalbh's market days, hears the whole saying said at the stone and carries it home the length of the island, telling it first at her own hearth to a household that keeps no stone and no gathering-ground of its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6049"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, VE 4,876** — *A north-western shepherd answers a trader with the saying*. A shepherd of the far north-western moor, asked by a passing trader what his own people hold of where they came from, answers with the third stone's four words, though he has never walked south to hear them said at Achadh a' Chalbh himself.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6050"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,880** — *Seathan's father tells him the waiting is part of the keeping* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan's father tells the boy that the bag on its peg has waited longer than any stone in the south, and that a thing worth keeping is worth keeping without asking each year whether the keeping has come to anything.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6047"><em>A boy of the keeper's hearth hears of the third stone</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,868</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6051"></a>**19 an Cèitean, VE 4,882** — *Seathan takes the bag over* (Tobar dhìreach). On his father's death Seathan takes the bag of two coals and the keeping in his twentieth year, and chooses, unlike his father before him, to keep gual teine near the hearth rather than carry it abroad.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6050"><em>Seathan's father tells him the waiting is part of the keeping</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,880</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6052"></a>**20 an Giblean, VE 4,885** — *A trader woman walks ten days to the column* (Achadh a' Chalbh). A woman of the northern shore walks ten days south by the drove-roads to trade hides for salt at the column, hears many households say the same words together, and carries the saying home with the salt.
- <a id="ev-EI-6053"></a>**22 am Màrt, VE 4,888** — *Seathan marries Caitir* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan takes Caitir, of a household two valleys east that keeps no coal of its own, and she comes to Tobar dhìreach knowing she marries a keeper and not only a husband.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6051"><em>Seathan takes the bag over</em>, 19 an Cèitean, VE 4,882</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6054"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, VE 4,890** — *Ciannait says the saying to her children by her own fire*. In the last winter of her life, her joints too cold-bitten for the walk to Achadh a' Chalbh, Ciannait says the third stone's saying once more to her children at her own hearth, tying it plainly to Aithris a' Chruthachaidh of the grass-people grown from the island's own ground.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6044"><em>The gathering at the column kept a second year, and a third</em>, 20 an Giblean, VE 4,857</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6055"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, VE 4,891** — *Ciannait dies at her own hearth*. Ciannait dies in her one and seventieth year at the hearth where she was born, and is buried, as her own kin have always been buried, without any coal of the vein given her in the ground, that custom never having reached so far south-west in her lifetime.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6054"><em>Ciannait says the saying to her children by her own fire</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, VE 4,890</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6056"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, VE 4,895** — *Ciannait's children keep the walk to the column after her* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Ciannait's children take up the walk to Achadh a' Chalbh in her stead, not every year but often enough that the fire at the pillar's foot never goes long unlit in their own generation, and the saying she gave them at her hearth goes on being said by mouths that never stood at the stone itself.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6057"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,896** — *Gual teine put into the pot itself* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan puts gual teine into the fire the line holds to be the mason's own, carried unbroken since Oidhche an Dealanaich, and it lies dark and cool through the flame as it lies in every other fire he has tried.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6053"><em>Seathan marries Caitir</em>, 22 am Màrt, VE 4,888</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0073a"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905** — *The fire in the fingers* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan of Clann na Ceiste, who has handled the coal of fire all his days to no end, snaps his fingers when a thought strikes him, and the coal-dust on his hand takes fire. He beats it out against his coat and is not burned. So the sixth coal is lit, by the fire that is in the hand itself.
- <a id="ev-EI-6501"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, VE 4,905** — *Seathan snaps his fingers on the doorstone* (Tobar dhìreach). On a warm evening Seathan, breaking gual teine into dust between his fingers and thinking of the mason and the lightning's crack, snaps his fingers without meaning to try anything, and the dust on his hand takes fire, red-gold, and leaves no mark on him.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0073a"><em>The fire in the fingers</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6057"><em>Gual teine put into the pot itself</em>, 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,896</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6502"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, VE 4,905** — *Seathan laughs until Caitir comes* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan sits on the doorstone laughing until his wife comes out to him, and tells her, before he tells anyone else, that the fire has been in his own hand the whole thirty years he carried it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073a"><em>The fire in the fingers</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6501"><em>Seathan snaps his fingers on the doorstone</em>, 30 an Lùnastal, VE 4,905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6503"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, VE 4,905** — *The telling at the hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan tells gual teine's waking at the recital on Oidhche an Dealanaich that same year, plainly, as he told it to Caitir, and the valley begins to call the sixth coal gual teine.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073a"><em>The fire in the fingers</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6502"><em>Seathan laughs until Caitir comes</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, VE 4,905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6504"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, VE 4,905** — *Caitir turns Seathan's hand over* (Tobar dhìreach). Caitir, coming to the door at Seathan's shout with her hands floury from baking, sits down beside him on the doorstone and turns his hand over herself to see that there is no mark on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073a"><em>The fire in the fingers</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6502"><em>Seathan laughs until Caitir comes</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, VE 4,905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6505"></a>**12 an Gearran, VE 4,906** — *The children carry gual teine's waking to their mother's kin* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan's children, having seen their father laughing on the doorstone, run to tell their mother's kin before they rightly understand what there is to tell, and the word goes to every hearth within a day's walk.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6504"><em>Caitir turns Seathan's hand over</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, VE 4,905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6506"></a>**10 an Cèitean, VE 4,907** — *The rainbow thrown into the northern sea again*. Seathan carries gual bogha-froise to the northern shore in the old custom and throws it into the swell, and wades in after it to find it as dark and salt-wet as it went in.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6505"><em>The children carry gual teine's waking to their mother's kin</em>, 12 an Gearran, VE 4,906</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6507"></a>**11 an Giblean, VE 4,910** — *Dressed-up tellings of the snap corrected*. Tellers far from Tobar dhìreach begin to have Seathan snap his fingers on purpose, as a fisherman tries a new knot, and are corrected by those nearer the hearth who heard from Caitir that there was no purpose in it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6504"><em>Caitir turns Seathan's hand over</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, VE 4,905</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6508"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,920** — *The rainbow tried at the river crossing* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan and Caitir carry gual bogha-froise down to the crossing where the silver still burns under the current, and hold it and then throw it, and it lies cold and ordinary among the wet stones the next morning.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6506"><em>The rainbow thrown into the northern sea again</em>, 10 an Cèitean, VE 4,907</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6509"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,920** — *Caitir's saying of the rainbow* (Tobar dhìreach). Caitir says, after the river trial, that the rainbow holds every spirit and so belongs wholly to none of them, a saying that afterward passes among Clann na Ceiste.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6508"><em>The rainbow tried at the river crossing</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,920</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6510"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, VE 4,921** — *Caitir goes with the rainbow to the sea and the river*. Caitir walks with Seathan to the northern shore and to the river crossing with gual bogha-froise, the only keeper's wife of the line remembered to have gone and not stayed by the pot.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6509"><em>Caitir's saying of the rainbow</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,920</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6511"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, VE 4,934** — *Seathan dies at his own hearth* (Tobar dhìreach). Seathan dies in his three-and-seventieth year at Tobar dhìreach, Poit an Teine burning near him, asking at the last to hold gual teine once more rather than the rainbow.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0073a"><em>The fire in the fingers</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,905</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6510"><em>Caitir goes with the rainbow to the sea and the river</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, VE 4,921</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6512"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, VE 4,934** — *The bag passes to Seathan's eldest son* (Tobar dhìreach). The bag, holding only the rainbow now, passes from Seathan's grave to his eldest son, a quiet man who never expected so great a charge while his father's hand was still warm.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6511"><em>Seathan dies at his own hearth</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, VE 4,934</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6513"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, VE 4,938** — *Caitir tries the rainbow once more* (Tobar dhìreach). Caitir, staying on at Tobar dhìreach after Seathan's death, tries the rainbow once more at the river for the comfort of doing something with it, and it lies as dark and unmoved as it lay in her husband's hand.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6511"><em>Seathan dies at his own hearth</em>, 13 an Lùnastal, VE 4,934</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6514"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,940** — *Caitir dies at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). Caitir dies in her three-and-seventieth year, the same age Seathan reached before her, and is buried beside him near Leac na Fèithe.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6513"><em>Caitir tries the rainbow once more</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, VE 4,938</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6515"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, VE 4,940** — *Caitir tries the rainbow once more at the river* (Abhainn ghorm). In the years after Seathan's death Caitir tries the rainbow once more at the river below the house, and puts it back in the bag without disappointment, having ceased to expect it to answer a woman who only wished it well.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6514"><em>Caitir dies at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 4,940</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6516"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, VE 4,951** — *The crowd at the column grows* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Word of gual teine's waking spreads beyond the hill country's own hearths, and people begin coming to Achadh a' Chalbh in tens and then in hundreds to hear the recital said at the column, camping about the stone rather than passing it by.
- <a id="ev-I-0074"></a>**17 an Giblean, VE 4,951** — *The gatherings at the column* (Cnoc ghorm). People come to the column at Cnoc ghorm in numbers. The post-holes of shelters for some hundreds lie about it, used and rebuilt many times. Whatever was said there was said to a crowd.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6516"><em>The crowd at the column grows</em>, 19 am Faoilleach, VE 4,951</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6517"></a>**18 an Cèitean, VE 4,960** — *A nephew of Seathan afraid of the crowd* (Achadh a' Chalbh). The young nephew of Seathan sent to say the Line at the column sits apart from the fires the day before, sick with fear of so many faces, until an old woman tells him that a story kept in one hearth is safe from nothing but changing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6518"></a>**20 an Gearran, VE 4,965** — *The first shelters built at the column* (Achadh a' Chalbh). The crowd that gathers to hear the recital builds the first low walls of turf and hide about Achadh a' Chalbh, taken down again when the telling ends, because no one yet thinks of the column's ground as a place a person lives.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6519"></a>**21 am Màrt, VE 4,970** — *Seathan's nephew gives the telling to a crowd* (Achadh a' Chalbh). Clann na Ceiste sends a nephew of Seathan's to Achadh a' Chalbh to say the recital naming gual teine to a hillside of strangers rather than a single hearth, and an old woman of the gathering tells him a story given to a crowd is safe from dying, whatever changes it gathers in the carrying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6512"><em>The bag passes to Seathan's eldest son</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, VE 4,934</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6520"></a>**19 an Giblean, VE 4,980** — *The telling slowed for the crowd* (Achadh a' Chalbh). For the crowd at the column the Line comes to be said more slowly, with a pause after each father's name long enough for those at the back to have it passed forward mouth to mouth.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6521"></a>**21 am Màrt, VE 5,000** — *The shelters at the column rebuilt* (Achadh a' Chalbh). The shelters at Achadh a' Chalbh are rebuilt so many times over on the footings of the ones before them that a household coming for the first time can see, in the worn hollows and packed earth, that others have stood there before it and will stand there after.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>.</span>

## The Years VE 5,001 – 5,324

- <a id="ev-I-0075"></a>**16 an Cèitean, VE 5,010** — *Tuam Cnoc dhìreach consecrated* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). A burial-ground grows about a place that none remembers hallowing. Its oldest graves are older than the oldest names that can be read there.
- <a id="ev-EI-6522"></a>**20 an Gearran, VE 5,020** — *The rainbow passed hand to hand at the column* (Achadh a' Chalbh). At a great telling at the column a keeper of the bag gives gual bogha-froise into the crowd, and it goes round from hand to hand by firelight through the whole night and comes back to him at dawn as dark as it went out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0074"><em>The gatherings at the column</em>, 17 an Giblean, VE 4,951</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6523"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, VE 5,030** — *The bag passes down the line of fathers* (Tobar dhìreach). The bag holding gual bogha-froise, passes down the line of fathers from Seathan's son, and a keeper whose name the recital keeps from strangers resolves to try it in the oak grove at Doire ghlas.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6519"><em>Seathan's nephew gives the telling to a crowd</em>, 21 am Màrt, VE 4,970</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6524"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, VE 5,050** — *The rainbow tried in the grove*. A keeper of Clann na Ceiste carries gual bogha-froise north to the oak grove at Doire ghlas and sits with it through a night by his own small fire as Diarmad once sat, waiting for any sign Coimhdeach na Fine gave before; the coal lies black and cold among the ash by morning, and the grove answers him nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0073"><em>Calbh Cnoc ghorm raised</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, VE 4,851</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6525"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, VE 5,067** — *Aoife's child born*. Aoife bears a living child after two she has already lost in their first winters, and lets herself believe, when it survives its own first winter thin but breathing steadily, that this one will live to walk; she sews it, for the first time, a coat cut to its own growing rather than one handed down.
- <a id="ev-EI-6526"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,068** — *Aoife sews a coat cut to the child's growing*. Aoife, trusting for the first time that a child of hers will live, sews in the last cold months a small coat cut to the child's own growing, a thing she had not let herself do for the two children before.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6525"><em>Aoife's child born</em>, 15 an t-Iuchar, VE 5,067</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0076"></a>**14 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,070** — *The black chip in the child's grave* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). A child is buried at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach with a sliver of the coloured coal closed in one hand. The sliver stains still the cloth it is kept in. No other piece of the vein is found with the dead of this age.
- <a id="ev-EI-6527"></a>**18 an Cèitean, VE 5,071** — *Aoife's child dies*. Aoife's child sickens in the spring and dies quietly in her arms, the third child she has lost and the first she does not hear cry out at the end, so that she says afterward she knew, before she was willing to know it, that this death would not be like the others.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6526"><em>Aoife sews a coat cut to the child's growing</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,068</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6528"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, VE 5,071** — *The child buried with the sliver of coal* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). Aoife closes into her dead child's hand the one sliver of an gual dathach her household still keeps, over her husband's mother's objection, and it is buried with the child at the western edge of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, the only piece of the vein put into the ground with the dead this age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0076"><em>The black chip in the child's grave</em>, 14 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,070</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6527"><em>Aoife's child dies</em>, 18 an Cèitean, VE 5,071</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6529"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, VE 5,071** — *Words between two households over the sliver*. Aoife's husband's mother says a hearth ought not give a piece of an gual dathach to the dead while the living have use for it, and there are words between the two households that neither afterward cares to keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0076"><em>The black chip in the child's grave</em>, 14 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,070</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6528"><em>The child buried with the sliver of coal</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, VE 5,071</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6530"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, VE 5,080** — *The graves begin to keep a line* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). The newer graves at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach's western edge begin, without any household deciding it, to be set in a row facing the northern mountains, each new grave drawn to the line the ones before it have already kept, until a household bringing its dead looks for the row before it looks for empty turf.
- <a id="ev-EI-6531"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, VE 5,080** — *A grave dug round an old swelling* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). A young man digging his grandfather's grave at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach proposes levelling an old unnamed swelling in his row's path, and is rebuked by an elder digger, who tells him no man may open a grave whose occupant he cannot name; the row bends round it instead.
- <a id="ev-EI-6532"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,090** — *An uncle forbids the levelling of an old grave* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). A young man digging his grandfather's grave at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach proposes to level an old swelling in the row's path, and his uncle forbids it: a man who cannot say whose grave he opens has no business opening it.
- <a id="ev-EI-6533"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, VE 5,110** — *Aoife dies* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). Aoife dies in her seventieth year, forty years after burying her child, and is carried to Tuam Cnoc dhìreach and laid in the row nearest the western edge where the child already lies, the row bending as it reaches her grave to keep clear of the old swelling beside it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6529"><em>Words between two households over the sliver</em>, 30 an Lùnastal, VE 5,071</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0077"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, VE 5,114** — *The rows at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). The graves at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach begin to be laid in rows, heads toward the central mountains. The first rows are straight. The later ones bend round older graves that no one will disturb.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6530"><em>The graves begin to keep a line</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, VE 5,080</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6531"><em>A grave dug round an old swelling</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, VE 5,080</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EI-6532"><em>An uncle forbids the levelling of an old grave</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,090</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6534"></a>**20 an Gearran, VE 5,150** — *The western face of the burial hill woven with bending rows* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). Seen from far enough off, the whole western face of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach shows no longer straight lines but a slow curved weaving of rows folding round the swellings no living hand made.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0077"><em>The rows at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, VE 5,114</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0078"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,170** — *The panther roads*. The great cats of the island are first seen to keep their roads, crossing the mountains by fixed ways at fixed seasons. Why they do so no one has learned.
- <a id="ev-EI-6535"></a>**21 am Màrt, VE 5,192** — *Beithir finds the cats' road in the snow* (Imrich nam Pantar). A herder of the central mountains follows three strayed ewes into a high saddle and finds a line of prints worn into the frozen turf on both sides of it, running straight where the ground gave the beast no cause to turn; his own hearth's elders tell him their fathers knew the same line and the same two turns of year it is kept in.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0078"><em>The panther roads</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6536"></a>**19 an Giblean, VE 5,195** — *An old man tells Beithir the cats keep their roads* (Imrich nam Pantar). The oldest man of Beithir's hearth tells him that his father and his father's father said the same of that saddle: the great cats of the mountains do not wander the high ground but cross it, at some seasons and not others.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0078"><em>The panther roads</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0079"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, VE 5,219** — *The crossing season kept* (Imrich nam Pantar). The hill-folk learn the panthers' seasons and keep off the high passes while the cats cross. The camps in the passes stand empty at the same point in every year.
- <a id="ev-EI-6537"></a>**18 an Cèitean, VE 5,220** — *The gatepost sign first cut* (Imrich nam Pantar). A household of the high valleys cuts a fresh mark into its gatepost at the turn of year the cats' smell and track return to the passes, and scrapes it away again once both are gone, so that a stranger walking the crossing weeks can read the closed season on every post without asking what the mark means.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-I-0079"><em>The crossing season kept</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 5,219</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6538"></a>**9 am Màrt, VE 5,222** — *Àirighean a' Bhealaich stand empty* (Àirighean a' Bhealaich). The herders' summer camps on the high passes are found stripped and shuttered at the same point in every year while the cats cross, a boy sent up in error by his father's lost count of days finding one already closed and coming down again with nothing worse than a wasted night's walk.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0079"><em>The crossing season kept</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 5,219</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6539"></a>**7 an Giblean, VE 5,225** — *The gatepost cut deep enough to read in the scraping* (Imrich nam Pantar). An old woman of the eastern slopes tells a new-married daughter that the crossing mark must be cut deep enough to be read even after it is scraped, so that a late-comer knows the season has been kept there before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0079"><em>The crossing season kept</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 5,219</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6540"></a>**8 an Giblean, VE 5,226** — *A boy sent up in error to a stripped shieling* (Àirighean a' Bhealaich). A boy sent up to winter sheep at a shieling in the crossing season, his father having lost the count of days in a wet spell, finds it already stripped and shuttered by households that read the signs, and comes down the same evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0079"><em>The crossing season kept</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, VE 5,219</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6541"></a>**10 am Màrt, VE 5,230** — *Thirty head lost to a broken custom* (Imrich nam Pantar). A herdsman of the lower slopes, trusting his own count of the year over his neighbours' gatepost signs, keeps his cattle ten days past the crossing's start and brings them down to find thirty head missing from the herd, torn on the ground above the track in a way no wolf of that country tears ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0078"><em>The panther roads</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6542"></a>**7 an Cèitean, VE 5,250** — *The cats turn back at the foothills* (Imrich nam Pantar). A family watching from a rise above the track sees the crossing cats turn from the eastern passes and go back down toward the western foothills for no cause the watchers can find, and the country reads the plain sign as a warning rather than let it pass unanswered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0078"><em>The panther roads</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6543"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,250** — *The households store double* (Imrich nam Pantar). On the strength of the turning cats the country stores double against a hard winter that no other sign has yet shown, cutting peat and laying by grain and dried meat past what the ordinary count of mouths at each hearth calls for; the winter that follows proves hard enough to repay the extra carrying.
- <a id="ev-EI-6544"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,251** — *The hard winter after the cats turned back*. The winter after the cats turn back lays snow to a grown man's waist in the lower valleys for the better part of two months, and every household that stored double says afterward the cutting and the carrying were worth it.
- <a id="ev-EI-6545"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, VE 5,271** — *A household scrapes its gatepost early* (Imrich nam Pantar). A household near the high passes, reading the geese's lateness as a slow season, scrapes its crossing mark bare a full ten days before the cats' smell returns to the saddle above it.
- <a id="ev-EI-6546"></a>**13 an Gearran, VE 5,272** — *Cairbre and ten set out* (Teallaichean a' Chladaich). Cairbre leads ten men inland from Teallaichean a' Chladaich, reasoning by the coast's own geese, which have not yet gone over in their numbers that autumn, that the crossing season has not yet begun; a household nearer the mountains has scraped its own gatepost clean on the same late reading and by the same error.
- <a id="ev-EI-6547"></a>**14 an Gearran, VE 5,272** — *The eleven do not come home* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Cairbre and the ten who went with him fail to reach the valley they set out for and do not return to the shore; no household along the mountains can say it saw them pass, and winter closes the high ground before any search can be made of it that year.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6546"><em>Cairbre and ten set out</em>, 13 an Gearran, VE 5,272</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0080"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272** — *Eleven lost on the panther road* (Cnoc àrsaidh). A party of eleven from the southern shore goes up into the hills near Cnoc àrsaidh in the crossing season and does not return. Years afterwards their bones are found along the line the cats use still.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6545"><em>A household scrapes its gatepost early</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, VE 5,271</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6546"><em>Cairbre and ten set out</em>, 13 an Gearran, VE 5,272</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EI-6547"><em>The eleven do not come home</em>, 14 an Gearran, VE 5,272</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6548"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272** — *Word comes of a failed harvest inland* (Teallaichean a' Chladaich). Word reaches Teallaichean a' Chladaich that kin settled two valleys further into the hills than the shore's people commonly go have had their harvest fail badly enough that they will not see the winter through unhelped, and Cairbre resolves to lead ten of his own hearth up to carry it down to them.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6547"><em>The eleven do not come home</em>, 14 an Gearran, VE 5,272</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6549"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,272** — *Suibhne born at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). A son is born to the household that keeps Poit an Teine and the bag of coals, a big child who closes his hand round a finger held out to him and will not readily let it go, so that they say of him he was born holding on; he is given the name Suibhne.
- <a id="ev-EI-6550"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, VE 5,273** — *Cairbre's wife watches the path thirty days* (Teallaichean a' Chladaich). Cairbre's wife keeps the twelfth day and the fourteenth and the twentieth on the rise above Teallaichean a' Chladaich, and by the thirtieth has stopped telling herself anything, and only watches.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0080"><em>Eleven lost on the panther road</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6548"><em>Word comes of a failed harvest inland</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6551"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, VE 5,274** — *Two springs of searching find nothing*. The shore and the kin the eleven had set out to help each try the high ground in the spring after they go missing, and again the spring after that, and both times come down with nothing to show for the walking but blistered feet and a country too wide to give up eleven men for the asking.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6550"><em>Cairbre's wife watches the path thirty days</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, VE 5,273</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6552"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, VE 5,285** — *Suibhne learns the Line standing* (Tobar dhìreach). Suibhne, a boy of the keeper's hearth, hears the whole of the Line said over him standing, as every keeper before him had heard it, and learns it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6549"><em>Suibhne born at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,272</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6553"></a>**9 an Gearran, VE 5,290** — *The bones found along the cats' line* (Cnoc àrsaidh). A drover's dog worries a length of bone out of the turf off the marked track at the proper close of a crossing season, and searchers over the following days gather a scatter of bone strung along roughly the same course the cats are known to keep, with nothing of what the eleven carried found among it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0080"><em>Eleven lost on the panther road</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6551"><em>Two springs of searching find nothing</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, VE 5,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6554"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, VE 5,290** — *The eleven buried where they were found* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Unable to say with certainty which bones belonged to which man, the southern shore buries the gathered dead together high on the mountain rather than divide them wrongly among separate graves, and keeps alongside Cairbre's name the plainer lesson the country had already made of the matter: that the crossing months keep a count of their own that no household's calendar has yet learned to keep exactly with it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0080"><em>Eleven lost on the panther road</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, VE 5,272</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6553"><em>The bones found along the cats' line</em>, 9 an Gearran, VE 5,290</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6555"></a>**10 am Màrt, VE 5,300** — *Ailean born to Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). A son is born to Suibhne of Clann na Ceiste at Tobar dhìreach, heavier in arm and leg than the women at his birth can readily match against memory, and slow to close his hand on a finger held out to him and slower to let it go, so that his mother says he was born holding on.
- <a id="ev-EI-6556"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,304** — *Ailean found by Poit an Teine for whole mornings* (Tobar dhìreach). Ailean, able to sit upright, is found by Poit an Teine for whole mornings together, not reaching for it or troubling it, only sitting near enough to feel its heat and watching the low flame.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6555"><em>Ailean born to Tobar dhìreach</em>, 10 am Màrt, VE 5,300</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6557"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, VE 5,306** — *Ailean grows slow of speech and broad of hand* (Tobar dhìreach). Ailean keeps to single words while children a season younger than him are stringing sentences, and some of his kin wonder aloud whether the line has thrown up a son too plain for the keeping, until his mother points to his hands, already broad at six years old, as proof enough of what manner of man he will be.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6556"><em>Ailean found by Poit an Teine for whole mornings</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, VE 5,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6558"></a>**26 an Gearran, VE 5,310** — *Ailean's mother answers the talk of his slowness* (Tobar dhìreach). Ailean's mother puts a stop to the kin's talk of a son too plain for the keeping, saying a slow tongue is no mark against a steady hand, and pointing to his hands.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6557"><em>Ailean grows slow of speech and broad of hand</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, VE 5,306</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6559"></a>**27 am Màrt, VE 5,312** — *Suibhne drops the rainbow from Binnean a' Chlachair* (Binnean a' Chlachair). In the second year of his keeping Suibhne climbs Binnean a' Chlachair and drops the rainbow from the height of his arm over the same steep side Fearghas used, and it falls to the stones without a flicker.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6555"><em>Ailean born to Tobar dhìreach</em>, 10 am Màrt, VE 5,300</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6560"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, VE 5,313** — *Suibhne lays the rainbow beside the burning silver* (Abhainn ghorm). Suibhne throws the rainbow into the river at the crossing where the silver still burns under the current, so that for a breath the two lie side by side, dark against bright, before the current carries it on.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6559"><em>Suibhne drops the rainbow from Binnean a' Chlachair</em>, 27 am Màrt, VE 5,312</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6561"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, VE 5,314** — *Suibhne will not try the rainbow by blood* (Tobar dhìreach). Suibhne tries the rainbow by the sea, the height, the river and the earth, but will not try it by blood, telling his wife a man ought not open his own hand for a coal that has shown it wants no single element.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6560"><em>Suibhne lays the rainbow beside the burning silver</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, VE 5,313</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6562"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, VE 5,316** — *Suibhne carries the rainbow to Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). In his four-and-fortieth year Suibhne walks the three days north to Doire ghlas with gual bogha-froise, the first keeper to bring it to the grove where Coimhdeach na Fine first spoke, and sits under the oaks a night and a day with it held loose in his open hand; it shows him no change of colour or warmth, and he carries it home cold.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6561"><em>Suibhne will not try the rainbow by blood</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, VE 5,314</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6563"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, VE 5,316** — *Suibhne says he doubts the rainbow will answer him* (Tobar dhìreach). Suibhne tells his own hearth, and not the recital, that he no longer knows whether a man ought to go on asking a question already asked in every way his own life can think to ask it; his son Ailean, sixteen years old, hears it among the last things of any length his father says on the matter.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6562"><em>Suibhne carries the rainbow to Doire ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, VE 5,316</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6564"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, VE 5,317** — *Ailean marries Lìobhan* (Tobar dhìreach). Ailean, seventeen, takes Lìobhan of a household two valleys west that keeps no coal of its own; she comes to Tobar dhìreach a bride of fifteen and is taught by Suibhne's widow, in the short time left to teach her, how Poit an Teine is fed and the bag kept and what is and is not said of it to a stranger.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6563"><em>Suibhne says he doubts the rainbow will answer him</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, VE 5,316</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6565"></a>**10 an Cèitean, VE 5,318** — *Suibhne dies of a fever* (Tobar dhìreach). Suibhne dies in his forty-sixth year of a fever that takes him inside a fortnight, with Ailean, eighteen years old and already the broadest man of that hearth, sitting with him through the last nights; the bag of two coals passes to Ailean, though no word of keeping is said over him yet.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6563"><em>Suibhne says he doubts the rainbow will answer him</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, VE 5,316</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EI-6566"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,318** — *Gormshuil born* (Tobar dhìreach). A daughter is born to Ailean and Lìobhan in the same wet autumn the household buries Suibhne, and is named Gormshuil for the blue of her eyes at birth, which her grandmother swears she has never seen come on so soon in any other child.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EI-6565"><em>Suibhne dies of a fever</em>, 10 an Cèitean, VE 5,318</a>.</span>
